item.title: Just How Historic Is the 2026 Election, Really? It’s an Overwhelming Victory for Democrats against All Odds
item.author: Lisa Graves
item.content:encoded: On Tuesday, the American people delivered the strongest possible rebuke of Donald Trump’s second term in what headlines called “historic,” “shellacking,” and a “rout.”Voters swept a new generation of Democrats into power in the U.S. Senate and House of Representatives, governors’ offices, state attorney general posts, state supreme court chambers, and more. They rejected not just Trump, but his loyalists and lackeys, treating the races like he was on the ballot–as he demanded.Before the ink was dry on the headlines, however, the apologists and cynics were already trying to spin the news. declared that this extraordinary blue wave was not a mandate. Ridiculous! A columnist claimed this was exactly what Trump wanted. Absurd! Republicans like Nikki Haley tried to cast the election as a matter of “candidate quality” rather than a repudiation of Trump’s destructive policies or an endorsement of Democrats’ inspiring campaigns. Try harder! In other words, the spinners want you not to believe what your eyes are seeing.As the great populist Jim Hightower once said: “The water won’t clear up until we get the hogs out of the creek.” In effect, the voters told Trump and his minions: “Quiet piggy!”The midterm election results really are a stinging rebuke. Even Ron DeSantis called it “an extinction-level event” for Republicans.What happened is an enormous grassroots feat, a massive determined effort by millions of people to impose a real check on Trump’s abuses of power and the havoc he has wreaked on American families and the world. More Americans turned out for this midterm election than any other since 1914, with the exception of the 2018 midterms–the only other time voters delivered a midway-point condemnation of Trump.Almost every state trended bluer, many by double digits. Almost every demographic voted Democratic, except white men. Even a majority of baby boomers went blue. Republicans still won a majority of white voters without college degrees, but they lost about 14% of that contingent, too. This shift is seismic, a nationwide earthquake.Let’s look at some of the results whose magnitude has not yet been fully appreciated.I know part of this story because, two years ago this week, staggered by Trump’s win over Kamala Harris, I took a deep dive into whether there was any chance Democrats could get power in either house of Congress to impose checks on his coming abuses of power. In 2024, Republicans won a trifecta: the presidency, the Senate, and the House. But they really had a “superfecta,” or quadfecta, because they had also captured the U.S. Supreme Court, and John Roberts had delivered by helping to sweep Trump back into power through inventing immunity from criminal prosecution for him and his so-called “official acts.”As a former Senate staffer, I looked at the Senate first. Every two years, about one-third of the U.S. Senate is up for re-election. As of January 2025, Democrats held only 45 seats, with two Independents (Bernie Sanders of Vermont and Angus King of Maine) caucusing with them.Republicans held 53 seats, meaning they could lose three Republicans on any vote and still break a tie with the help of Vice President JD Vance. He had cast the deciding vote that installed the incompetent Pete Hegseth at DOD, despite the allegations of boozing and rape.The prospect of Democrats retaking the Senate majority back then looked bleak.For example, they would have to hold a Senate seat in a state Trump won in 2024: Jon Ossoff’s in Georgia, which was rated R+1 in the Cook Partisan Voting Index. They would also have to retain three seats where the Democrat was retiring, meaning no incumbent with a name recognition advantage: New Hampshire (D+2), Minnesota (D+3), and Michigan (R+0). They needed to hold all four of those seats just to maintain the status quo of being the minority party in the Senate.To get to a bare majority, they would then need to pick up four additional seats. In reality, they needed five to build a working majority and avoid another Joe Manchin or Kyrsten Sinema style of policy betrayals (a role John Fetterman would soon appear poised to play).The list of potential seat gains seemed almost entirely impossible, but, as we know now, that was not so:It had been 30 years since elected a Democrat to the Senate, but Troy Jackson just won. The race was rated D+4, hardly a sure thing, and Leonard Leo–who hand-picked Brett Kavanaugh for Trump’s SCOTUS nomination–fundraised for the incumbent Republican senator, Susan Collins, at his mansion in 2019 after she voted for Kavanaugh; Leo directed millions toward helping her this year.In , after Trump knocked out incumbent John Cornyn, schoolteacher James Talarico won big. The seat was rated R+6, and no Democrat had won a U.S. Senate race there since 1988. Voters also ousted Greg Abbott as governor in favor of Gina Hinojosa and Democrats swept almost every other statewide office. Ted Cruz is up for reelection in 2030 and will face an electorate that has shown its willingness to blunt Republican control in the wake of Trump’s ICE brutality and draconian state abortion restrictions. Plus, Texas turning blue really changes the Electoral College strategy for the 2028 presidential election and beyond.In (R+1) Trump pushed Thom Tillis out of running again after Tillis opposed his “Big, Beautiful Bill” due to the coming Medicaid cuts designed to enrich billionaires even further. The seat had been held for decades by the bigoted Jesse Helms, followed by other Republicans. Populist Democrat Roy Cooper won handily.In (R+5), Sherrod Brown kicked John Husted’s now-infamous ass, ousting JD Vance’s replacement. Ohio also elected Dr. Amy Acton governor. Her opponent spent millions siding with a child molester–embraced by Trump and Vance, too. Democrats also retained and gained a seat on the Ohio Supreme Court. (R+6) turned blue and elected a Democrat–Special Olympics gold medalist Josh Turek–to the Senate for the first time since Tom Harkin in 2008. Ds swept other state offices, too. Sen. Chuck Grassley, now 93, is still planning to run for re-election in 2028.Dr. Annie Andrews flipped (R+8) after Trump backed the late Sen. Lindsey Graham’s sister “Darline!” Before Trump loyalist Lindsey, the seat had been held for nearly 50 years by Dixiecrat Strom Thurmond, who once ran for president under the motto “Segregation Forever.” Andrews is the first woman elected to the U.S. Senate in South Carolina history. (R+8) elected their first Democrat to the U.S. Senate in 93 years, shifting more than 21 points compared to the last race toward Democrat Adam Hamilton. Voters also threw out vote-suppressor Kris Kobach as Kansas Attorney General, replacing him with Democrat Chris Mann.Alaska (R+6) is still too close to call, though Democrat Mary Peltola leads despite Trump’s efforts to stop the election from happening. In Mississippi (R+11), Democrat Scott Colom currently leads Cindy Hyde-Smith (who I call Confederate Barbie). If Colom prevails, he will be the first Black Senator elected there since the Reconstruction-era state legislature chose Hiram Revels in 1870 to serve a one-year term replacing Jefferson Davis, the president of the confederacy. Revels was the first Black U.S. senator in American history. Mississippi was on no politico’s bingo card for a win in 2026, but Colom and the voters did not give up and are still fighting to have all the votes counted.The House of Representatives looked barely more promising as a potential firewall against Trump’s agenda and extremism. Of the 435 House seats, only about 30 were considered competitive and Democrats would have to keep half of them to just hold steady at 214. Then, they would need to pick-up at least four more to get to a majority.So Trump began pressuring Republican-controlled states to redraw their congressional maps to cheat by helping him make it harder for Democrats to get the seats needed to counter him and conduct investigations.He wasn’t acting alone. The Roberts Court jumped in to help him and fellow Republicans.Earlier this spring, the Republican appointees on the nation’s highest court gutted the Voting Rights Act (VRA) and long-standing precedents to allow extreme partisan gerrymandering, even when doing so dilutes minority representation and bleaches out Black and Latino representation.Republicans used mathematical precision to gerrymander more Democrats into fewer districts in order to maximize their own seat totals. In this cycle, Republican-controlled state legislatures or redistricting entities changed 12 maps to give Republicans an advantage, including Texas (+5 seats), Florida (+4), North Carolina (+1), and Ohio (+2).The Roberts Court then ratified Texas’s steal (over objections by the lower court) and gave Republicans a shot at three more in Louisiana, Alabama, and Tennessee–for a total of 15–through its ruling, which neutered section 2 of the VRA. California countered with its own effort to flip 5 seats, while other states’ efforts–like those in Missouri, Virginia, Indiana, and Illinois–to change their maps were stalled.If the scheme had prevailed and Republicans won the targets of the maps they rewrote while holding the rest, they would have controlled 234 seats in Congress. They could have easily weathered defections from more than a couple of members, like Thomas Massie, over major issues such as the Epstein Transparency Act, which mandates the disclosure of investigative files implicating Trump and others in sex crimes.The American people resoundingly, resiliently, and even joyously rejected this scheme.Right now, Democrats are on track to hit a near-super majority, with 260 members.Republicans picked up only a few of the seats they re-mapped to steal. This wipeout is as significant as the New Deal wave, without the presidency… at least not yet.Democrats will be able to pass legislation to help the American people, which Trump will probably veto and drag his party to further ruin. They will also have the power to investigate the financial and moral costs of the vast corruption and destruction his administration has unleashed. The Senate can also block his nominees to the judiciary and other posts and both houses can make the case for bold reforms of the Roberts Court and much, much more.It’s a brand new day and, as Nina Simone so beautifully sang, I’m “Feeling Good.”What I’m also singing and savoring:And a trio of songs about surviving: by Destiny’s Child, by Gloria Gaynor, and . Although the rising fascism and incompetence of Trump and his enablers have tested our resolve, we must keep remembering that We the People are stronger than them.Get the full receipts every Monday in The Cover-UpAccountability starts with the record. COURIER’s new Contradictions Tracker compares testimony to the Epstein files, with every source linked. Follow along every Monday in The Cover-Up.

item.title: Kings Give Up On First-Round Pick After 83 Games, Trade Him For Basically Nothing
item.author: Giri Nathan
item.content:encoded: Not all franchises are made equal. Some are widely understood by their peers to be operated by dullards. These imbalances are clear to everyone—fans, analysts, other executives—if not to the dullards themselves. Is it bullying whenever the Oklahoma City Thunder do business with, say, the Sacramento Kings? Maybe it is.During the 2025 NBA Draft, these two teams kicked off the first phase of this saga. The Kings sent a top-16 protected pick belonging to the San Antonio Spurs; the Thunder sent the No. 24 pick. The Kings then used that pick to select Nique Clifford, a versatile 6-foot-5 prospect. The knock on Clifford was his age—already 23 at draft night—but he was considered a good athlete with positional size, feel, and ball skills. After a solid rookie season, he was a modest source of hope on a Sacramento roster that badly needed any. Any evaluation of Clifford would also have to factor in that he was playing under full-time head coach Doug Christie, who is the NBA franchise equivalent of swapping on the donut tire on your car and then taking it on a cross-country road trip. Christie had poor Clifford playing point guard for stretches of the season, struggling to make plays out of isolation. But at least Clifford was in no rush to prove himself, having joined a play-in franchise on a clear downward trajectory which included conducting confusing trades for middling players.Alas, Clifford just couldn't keep up with the furious pace of innovation in Sacramento. Just 16 months after the Kings acquired him, Clifford had slipped out of the rotation. On Sunday, they traded him back to the Thunder, and in return received two-second round picks. Particularly strange is the timing of the trade. What was Sacramento's rush to move on from the sophomore? The 1-9 Kings are headed nowhere but hell. They have a lively point guard now in Darius Acuff Jr., who has been happily taking on galactic usage; their best wing, Keegan Murray, finally returned from an ankle injury yesterday. If anything, now is the time to properly test out all their rookie-scale players and assess their quality.

item.title: Nvidia CEO Admits To Affair With An Accused Spy For The Chinese Government
item.author: Patrick Redford
item.content:encoded: On Sunday, Nvidia announced that it was opening an investigation into CEO Jensen Huang after he admitted to an affair with a Singapore-based data-center company executive named Alice Huang (no relation), whom U.S. officials say is also working as a spy for Chinese state intelligence. Given the size of Nvidia, as well as its strategic centrality to the intense AI buildout competition between the U.S. and China, Huang might be the single most desirable person in the tech industry, if not the whole world, for Beijing to honeypot. According to reporting around the matter, it seems like they got what they came for.We must begin with the crux of the issue, which is the matter of why Nvidia is in such a central position. AI software companies like OpenAI and Anthropic have gotten significantly more media attention because they make consumer products and engage in marketing rhetoric about their potential to create the machine god, but Nvidia is the company that has made the most actual money during the ongoing AI boom. Nvidia makes chips, supposedly the best of all the chips, on which every big-time software company built its flagship platforms a few years ago. This has made Nvidia the second-biggest publicly traded company in the world, and has made its founder Jensen Huang fabulously wealthy and quite the influential figure.It's also made the Santa Clara–based Nvidia the most critical part of the U.S. strategic plan to assert global AI dominance, by which I mean dominance over China, its principal competitor in the field. American trade policy forbids Nvidia from selling its best stuff to Chinese companies: U.S. policymakers want American companies to build the biggest and best data centers and create AI software that can most effectively and profitably book a flight for you, tell you some stuff you love about your kid, or conduct microtargeted drone assassinations of restive labor organizers.

item.title: Patriots Emit Foul Odor In Blowout Loss To Packers
item.author: Luis Paez-Pumar
item.content:encoded: Things have to be really bad for the New England Patriots if even Christian Gonzalez is dropping a stinker. The All-Pro cornerback has been one of the most consistent players on a Pats team that has struggled to find consistency at other positions, but Sunday against the Green Bay Packers, Gonzalez was just like many of his teammates: overwhelmed and outmatched in a 45-27 loss that was functionally over by the third quarter.This was the worst performance of Gonzalez's pro career since he entered the NFL in 2023. Against Green Bay's receiving duo of Matthew Golden and Christian Watson, the league's highest-paid cornerback was helpless, consistently getting beat on deep routes and losing one or both in coverage for touchdowns. According to Next Gen Stats, Gonzalez gave up a total of 10 catches for 187 receiving yards on Sunday, the most of his career and the third-most of any player this season. He had given up a total of 196 receiving yards across his first six games. On Green Bay's second TD of the day, Gonzalez and teammate Marcus Jones both covered Watson as he ran to the corner, leaving Golden wide open. Late in the third quarter, Gonzalez over-leveraged toward the outside against Watson, who just ran a skinny post and essentially walked into the end zone to make the score 40-14."I mean, they just got the best of me today,” Gonzalez said after the loss. “I mean, this is pro football. They got good receivers like every team. So, they got the best of me today. Move on from it and be ready for next week.” His head coach Mike Vrabel was a little more pointed in his postgame comments: "When your best players don’t play good, you don’t have much of a chance in this league. So, we expect a lot more. He expects a lot more. We need more from him and everybody else."

item.title: NVIDIA’s Perfect Storm Swirl Around Trump and the AI Industry
item.author: Josh Marshall
item.source: Josh Marshall – TPM – Talking Points Memo
item.content:encoded: Last month I had a conversation with a high ranking AI executive who told me that the fundamental reason for the U.S. lead over China in AI development was U.S. access to high-performance NVIDIA processors. The Biden administration placed export controls on those chips targeting China back in 2022. The Trump administration sort of loosened those controls though, for a variety of reasons, that shift in policy hasn’t translated into that much actual change in practice. This struck me at the time: this is a wildly anti-China administration; it’s a wildly pro-AI administration which premises everything on the need to maintain a strategic AI edge over China; but it’s more open to allowing China access to these chips that are central to U.S. dominance in AI? How can that possibly make sense?This conversation has been on my mind for the last couple weeks as we’ve learned more and more about the spy scandal enveloping NVIDIA co-founder and CEO Jensen Huang. To bring you up-to-date, yesterday, NVIDIA’s board announced that it would investigate Huang’s relationship with Alice Huang (no relation), who U.S. intelligence believes is a Chinese spy. This came shortly after Jensen Huang admitted in an email to NVIDIA employees (immediately made public) that he had carried on an extramarital affair with Alice Huang.

item.title: Judge Plans To Appoint Special Master To Probe Trump DOJ Misconduct
item.author: David Kurtz
item.content:encoded: The DOJ’s Absurd Caddyshack MomentThe D.C. golf course case continues to be a surprise contender for the long-awaited but elusive judicial branch showdown with the Trump administration over its chronic defiance of federal judges.In an order over the weekend, U.S. District Judge Ana C. Reyes said she intends to appoint former D.C. U.S. Attorney Jessie K. Liu as a special master “to investigate whether Department of Justice or Department of the Interior counsel have committed ethical violations” in a lawsuit to block Trump’s renovation of the East Potomac Golf Course.Reyes has been outraged at the Trump administration after deferring to it early in the case only to have it burn her later — a common pattern over the past 22 months of Trump II. An extensive tree-cutting operation on the golf course over the Columbus Day weekend was the proximate trigger for Reye’s ire, but a series of representations made to her in open court and in court filings have proven to be misleading at best and downright false at worst, she has found.Liu’s investigation of Trump administration attorneys, including Stan Woodward, the No. 3 official at DOJ, will cover the period through Oct. 31, according to Reyes’ order, which offers this bio of Liu:Ms. Liu served as the United States Attorney for the District of Columbia from 2017 to 2020, the same office in which she previously served as an assistant U.S. attorney. In addition, she has held senior positions at the Justice Department. These include deputy assistant attorney general in the Civil Rights Division; counsel to the deputy attorney general on national security issues; and deputy chief of staff for the National Security Division. Ms. Liu also served as deputy general counsel of the U.S. Department of the Treasury. In addition, Ms. Liu has been a partner at several international law firms. She is currently a partner at Liu Shur Kravis LLP.Reyes gave the parties until Friday to raise any objections to Liu’s appointment (which will be at the government’s cost).Trump DOJ Watch: Shitshow EditionIn addition to serving as a sword against Trump foes and a shield for his friends, the Trump DOJ under Attorney General Todd Blanche is an absolute zoo: first told the White House in early October that she planned to resign as head of the Civil Rights Division after the election, but demanded that she be fired after he was displeased by her Oct. 18 appearance on “60 Minutes,” CBS News reports: “Justice Department officials were able to stall for time and allow her to proceed with her plans to resign after the election was over.”, who was forced out as the assistant attorney general for the National Security Division, was called “Eisenblock” behind his back by then-Trump DOJ official , who now sits on the Third Circuit, Bloomberg reports: “Blanche briefly thought that was his actual surname before continuing using the moniker …”The resignation of Miami U.S. Attorney may not have that dramatic of an immediate effect: “Many of the office’s most sensitive investigations were already being overseen by a top Blanche deputy, …” the NYT reports.Associate Attorney General ’s “willingness to put his name behind controversial legal actions had led some officials to joke behind his back that his initials really stand for Sign Whatever,” the WSJ reports.The Retribution: Post-Blowout EditionReeling from his midterm defeat, President Trump began threatening the new Democratic majority in Congress with imprisonment two months before it even takes office.In two Truth Social posts over the weekend, Trump labelled as “extortion” Democratic threats of impeachment and promises of congressional oversight and demanded the Trump DOJ investigate: “By copy of this statement, I am ordering the Department of Justice to look into this criminal act, immediately! President DONALD J. TRUMP”The Retribution: NYT EditionThe Trump DOJ considered naming the NYT as an indicted co-conspirator in its third prosecution of former FBI Director James Comey.In addition to all the grubby political retribution reasons for targeting the NYT, the Trump DOJ was desperately trying to get around a statute of limitations problem with charging Comey, the NYT reports: “The department’s consideration of treating The Times as a conspirator appeared to be an attempt to connect the Oct. 5, 2016, article with subsequent coverage by The Times involving Mr. Comey in a way that they contend could extend the statute of limitations.”Late-stage radicalization and instability have characterized the actions and mood of autocrats in decline. We are seeing a version of it taking shape in the White House now. The Republican wipeout in the elections is prompting a dangerous reaction in a leader whose personality cult is shrinking and fading and whose foreign patrons are taking advantage of his weakness to make their influence over him more visible.The Korematsu or Dred Scott of Our Time“There are some opinions that I hope in my lifetime will get overturned. The immunity case is one of them.”—Trump v. U.S., which cloaked the president in a broad grant of immunity from criminal prosecutionTrump DOJ Dismisses CA Election CaseIn a pissy filing, the Trump DOJ dismissed its lawsuit to force California election officials to segregate and not count the mail-in ballots of people who showed up on the department’s dubious list of 20,000 alleged noncitizens. The administration had suffered keys loses in the case at the district court, appeals court, and Supreme Court in the days before the election.Kris Kobach Defeated In Kansas!Longtime TPM fave Kris Kobach — an OG voter fraud bamboozler who later turned his attention to requiring proof of citizenship to register to vote — lost his re-election bid for Kansas attorney general.More State Level Election Tidbits and TriviaNot since Watergate … or Truman: “2026 will be the largest year for net gain in state legislative seats for Democrats since the 1974 Watergate Wave. As a percentage of seats, though, it’s looking like it’ll be the highest since Harry Truman’s election in 1948,” according to Chaz Nuttycombe, executive director of State Navigate.: Democrats gained six new trifectas and broke five Republican ones. Heading into the election, Republicans held trifectas in 23 states, Democrats in 16. Coming out of the election, Democrats hold 22 trifectas and Republicans have 17, with Alaska still pending.A rare cameo by the Whig Party: “In New York, Democrats are on track for their biggest state Senate majority since 1846, when they were running against the Whigs,” Politico reports.The Trump administration is allegedly engaged in chain refoulement, the unlawful practice of using third countries to do the dirty work of returning immigrants to their country of origin when U.S. courts or immigration judges have barred their deportations, according to a NYT report:But a New York Times investigation found that this program results in many of them being pushed back to the very countries where the Trump administration itself cannot legally send them. Some of the United States’ foreign partners have made clear that will happen. And when it does, the Trump administration continues sending planes full of deportees.The Times identified more than 110 people who had court-ordered protections and were handed over to foreign governments, only to then be passed on to home countries where they risked torture, sexual abuse or persecution — risks that have been validated by American courts.Rescued From the Memory Hole!The new Democratic majority in the House will bring the Jan. 6 memorial plaque honoring defenders of the Capitol up from the basement to which House Republicans had relegated it.

item.title: *The Week in 15 Selections*
item.content:encoded: One million years have passed since the last newsletter (7 days). Millennial Optimism is back. Texas is Blue. The Iowa Governor was a Tumblr hottie. Mississippi (Mississippi!) is on the verge of electing a black democrat to Senate. The leaves are falling, and the sky is dark in the afternoon. On to the links. There are so many interesting things to read and see this week: I am thinking again about this Giamatti quote about baseball because the Brewers won the World Series and now we must face winter alone yet again.“[Baseball] breaks your heart. It is designed to break your heart. The game begins in the spring, when everything else begins again, and it blossoms in the summer, filling the afternoons and evenings, and then as soon as the chill rains come, it stops and leaves you to face the fall alone”

item.title: The Bears Beat The Bucs With One Hand Tied Behind Their Backs
item.author: Lauren Theisen
item.content:encoded: Sunday night's Bucs-Bears game possessed the major ingredients necessary for a Chicago fan freakout. Franchise quarterback Caleb Williams looked lost for much of the action, throwing four interceptions and stalling on three second-half three-and-outs. The team as a whole, meanwhile, surrendered a first-half 17-3 lead, allowing the game-tying touchdown following a fumble in the final stages of the fourth quarter. But the concerns one would have about the Bears' offense feel relatively minor today, because despite all their errors, a buzzer-beating Cairo Santos field goal and a stout defensive performance allowed Chicago to notch their fourth straight win, 27-24, improving to 7-2 as they fight for first place in the NFL's toughest division.The first nine minutes at Soldier Field were a party. The Buccaneers, entering the game as clear underdogs but coming off their two best outings of the season, got steamrolled, allowing a pair of Williams TD passes while mustering just six yards of their own. From that point on, however, everything became a struggle. Williams chucked a pick near the end zone to conclude a drive, then tossed another on his very next chance when he tried and failed to loft the ball out of bounds to avoid a sack. Before halftime arrived, he'd gift a third pass to the defense, making a silly decision to just huck the ball forward under pressure. Watching from afar, it felt like Williams's early success had put him in a consequence-free mindset on the field, and in his postgame it did very much sound like confidence was the culprit."I'm going to throw until I can't throw anymore," Williams said. "That's how I live. I work my tail off to be in this position. I'll never not throw the ball. I could throw 100 picks in one game. ... That's how I grew up. That's who I am. I don't get gun-shy."

item.title: Winners of the 2026 Photomicrography Competition
item.author: Jason Kottke
item.content:encoded: Like what?! You can check out photographer Ole Bielfeldt’s behind-the-scenes process on Instagram; he built a whole custom rig to capture this composite image.The biggest challenge was speed and lighting.The printhead, in the printer, moves at a very high speed over the paper. Simultaneously, the ink droplets get injected at around 20 m/s. So to capture the ink droplets mid air and get my lens close enough, this required me to build a custom setup where, instead of the printhead moving over the paper, the paper moved below the printhead. This allowed me to keep the nozzles in focus while printing.As the max shutter speed of 1/8000s on my camera is way too slow, I used a high speed flash setup. Here the flash acts as the effective shutter, freezing the droplets mid air. I then used focus stacking to capture the depth of the scene.

item.title: Elderly golfer shits the bed on 60 Minutes
item.author: Jeff Tiedrich
item.source: everyone is entitled to my own opinion
item.content:encoded: What was the point of that? What were Preznit Fuckwit’s handlers imagining they were going to accomplish, by putting him on 60 Minutes for all the world to see? Was it to remind everyone that Donny is still the Big Boy President? That he wasn’t bent or bowed by the disastrous midterms? That he’s still got what it takes to sit behind the Big Boy Desk in the Oval Bordello, and run the show?Whatever Donny’s minders were hoping for, it didn’t happen. Dear Leader was so befuddled, and so compromised — both cognitively and ethically — that even a complete lightweight like Ross Fucking Douthat was able to nail him to the wall on corruption.Ross Douthat: “Here’s what I wanna understand. So your son manages or helps manage a cryptocurrency company called World Liberty Financial. You are a co-owner of that company.”Donny: Douthat: “Right? That’s correct, right? This company is also partially owned by investors connected to the government of the United Arab Emirates. I think if I told you that story and it was about the Biden family, if I said Joe Biden is the part owner of a company and it has all of these investments from the Middle East, you would say, ‘That sounds corrupt,’ right—”Donny dissembles for a bit, trying to explain why his actual corruption is good, while Sleepy Joe Brandon’s imaginary corruption is , but Douthat’s having none of it.Douthat: “But then why do you need the money? Why not just divest? Walk away—”Boom, there it is. Donny don’t need this tainted money. He’s already obscenely wealthy, so why doesn’t he just walk away from it, and not even give the It’s a concept so simple that even Clownstick von Douthat — the Face That Launched A Thousand Dumbfuck Columns — gets it. But Donny get it, and he launches into another incoherent explanation about why it’s totes cool for him rake in billions off of some dodgy fake-money factory he co-owns with his felonious failsons and also the United Arab Emirates.Ross once again cuts him off. Douthat: “But companies that are invested in by people in foreign countries, it seems like you could just walk away from that and then, you know, and then you would not be accused of corruption, right?”Bro, Ross Douthat is doing you a solid. He’s giving you an out. Just say But the concept of ‘how about you just don’t be corrupt?’ is so alien to Donny that he has no fucking clue what Douthat is talking about. But this money goes up to eleven! Why would anyone walk way from it? Douthat: “There’s a Forbes story that said that your net worth went up by $3 billion since you—”Donny: “Well, so did everyone’s”Douthat: “My net worth did not go up by $3 billion.”Donny: “Well, you should’ve had stock.”Douthat: Even Ross is taken aback by Donny’s tone-deaf defense of his own naked greed.While We the People still struggle to pay for basic goods and services, Dear Leader is out here about how much he’s enriched himself off of taxpayer dollars. Oh, and if your net worth didn’t go up as much as Donny’s did? Well then, it sucks to be you, bro. Maybe you should have done some insider stock trading, like he did. Show some initiative! Can you imagine if this 60 Minutes interview had aired the Sunday the midterms, and not after? How many additional seats would the Democrats have picked up? Ten? Twelve? All of them?January 3rd can’t come soon enough. We need a Democratic House and Senate to investigate Donny’s fuckery, and put a stop to as much of it as they can.Of course, Preznit Fuckwit that accountability is coming for him, and he’s reacting the only way he knows. He’s a penny-ante little mobster, so he immediately starts barking out penny-ante little threats. Of course, every seedy little mob boss needs a seedy little mob lawyer — and so Donny sent Muggsy Blanche over to CNN’s State of the Union, to do his best to intimidate the incoming Democratic Congress. Dana Bash: “But I do want to ask you about another thing that that president said. He said that the Democratic lawmakers are extortionists, and they should be imprisoned. Is that a possibility?”Todd Blanche: [long pause] Well, it depends on what the— the— the crime is and what they’ve done.”Free clue for Stammerin’ Todd: isn’t a crime — what it is, is lawmakers doing their Constitutionally-mandated job to root out corruption in the executive branch. It’s what the outgoing Republican Congress should have been doing all along. Todd knows , too.But Todd’s caught between a rock and an overfull diaper. The Boss wants him to go on the Sunday shows, goddammit, and scare the shit out of the Democrats — and so he has no choice but to show up on CNN and try his best to sound all threatening and stuff, and then sweat and stammer when Dana Bash asks the simple question: It’s all a cheap dog-and-pony show, and Todd knows , too.January 3rd is coming. Accountability is coming.Hakeem Jeffries: “I am a hard yes on the Hegseth resolution. The so-called Secretary of Defense has abused his power, undermined our national security, and engineered this reckless and costly war of choice in Iran, which has skyrocketed prices on the American people and made the country less safe. Pete Hegseth has got to go.”Look, no way am I on Team Jeffries. I do not want him to be Speaker of the House. But it’s nice to hear him be unequivocally on the right side of an issue, for a change.Well, since we’re down at the bottom of the post, we might as well do some Daily Claudia, right?Here’s a triptych from down at our lake on September 1, 2018.Have a great Monday, everyone.here’s your daily reminder that I can be found on Blue Sky at this link.this is going to be my closing message for the foreseeable future: do what you need to do to keep sane. if that means you need to disengage with my daily posts for a while, I get it. this community of ours will still be here when you return.to all the people who have signed on in the days since the election, . settle in as we all try to deal with the shitfuckery that’s ahead of us.we are all in this together, and we are all here for each other.

item.title: Why Wouldn’t NC State Hire Philip Rivers?
item.author: Ray Ratto
item.content:encoded: One imagines Philip Rivers in his fortress of solitude, away from his platoon of children and contemplating what to do with his winter now that his St. Michael Catholic High School team has been knocked out of the Alabama high school playoffs. Then it hit him: .Of course, it didn't happen that way, because the former quarterback's name has been the one most linked with the Raleigh job since Dave Doeren got tagged and bagged in late October. The possibility of him stepping into the gig was the principal discussion point in Rivers's postgame presser after St. Michael lost to Glenwood School on Friday night. It had been considered the est of for weeks, in fact, and Rivers had already been elevated to First Candidate In Training when his son Gunner (of course that is his name), who had been Rivers's quarterback at St. Mike's, committed to NC State.The presumption here is that Rivers's prosciutto-thin coaching résumé—in mentioning his six seasons at St. Mike, we have covered all of it—has been trumped by his ability to pry open donor pockets and make the Wolfpack relevant again in the bloated ACC. And when we say "again," we mean "as a big spender in a landscape where 'big' is $40 million a year rather than $20 million." Doeren made a point of describing the limitations that such a barebones budget played on the school's chances of being noticed, and the school responded with a simple, You're absolutely right about that, Dave-O. Now get out.

item.title: Bad news for kinky Brits
item.author: Samantha Cole
item.content:encoded: Good Monday morning. Last week, the UK imposed one of the strictest, most vague (and therefore overly broad) new laws around pornography in recent memory. Recording yourself having consensual kinky sex in private could come with jail time, as could watching other people do it. And sex workers are the ones to feel the repercussions of bad laws like these first, of course, with many reporting content disappearing from their online stores en masse. Keep reading to learn more about what it covers, and how creators are responding. “I adore breath play. I love being strangled, suffocated and drowned, and I love strangling and suffocating others. Waterboarding: that’s my favourite,” Melissa Todd, a UK-based writer and sex worker, told me. “Many women do: it really isn’t only horrid men forcing us to do these dreadful depraved acts. Interrupting oxygen supply produces the most intense sensation of euphoria. I enjoy it in my private life, and I offer it in sessions too.” she and anyone else in the UK distributing or possessing certain types of choking, suffocation, breath play, strangulation and a bunch of other types of porn — even if it’s just recorded in the privacy of their homes and not for sale on a porn site — could face up to five years in prison. This is, predictably, already a huge mess for sex workers. Adult creators watched platforms remove hundreds of their videos — even when the creators thought they were in compliance with the law. These creators say they were blindsided by the removals, since the content didn’t seem to violate the law at all. Creators are reporting one platform in particular, Clips4Sale, is purging content with little notice, “a precautionary measure,” with videos disappearing in the hundreds.“Of course, we were all aware of the new Act coming in and prepared accordingly, but not for anything at this scale. We've had nothing since and they've been tweeting as normal,” adult creator Sophia Truee said. Clips4Sale launched in 2003 and caters heavily to fetish content. “It's a huge blow to this area of the industry, and I can only hope things will be communicated soon. We, as creators, understand how difficult it is to be a content site in this current climate, but communication has not been prioritized,” Truee said, noting that this is happening right before the holidays, with Black Friday being one of the most popular times for creators selling content. “For many, this will be devastating, as over 20 years of the work will have just been wiped.” Important update for our RSS fans: If you’re a paid subscriber using our full text RSS feed and don’t want these newsletters included in your feed, you can now replace the feed’s URL, which usually looks like 404.feed.press/private?key=XXXX, with 404.feed.press/no-newsletters?key=XXXX instead. Questions? Reply here or email and we’ll try to help ya out.! Following widespread backlash, Meta announced last week it’s putting a planned update of its commercial terms of use on pause. The terms would have required business accounts to allow Meta to “use any content from such domains, web pages, or URLs to provide, develop, improve, research, train, and maintain the integrity of” Meta’s products. The new terms were initially set to go into effect on October 30, but after outcry from journalists and users who didn’t want Meta reaching far beyond Instagram and Facebook and into their websites to suck up their work as training data for its generative AI products, Meta announced it was pushing the change to November 20. Now, it’s on hold entirely. . Archaeologists discovered the oldest direct evidence of psychoactive cannabis use in a Siberian tomb that dates back 2,800 years and was the site of human and horse sacrifices. During excavations of the tomb, a team found more than 1,400 cannabis seeds scattered around the remains of several Iron Age individuals, and even identified cannabinoids—including the active compound tetrahydrocannabinol (THC)—in a person’s preserved hair. Though humans cultivated cannabis for many millennia before the Iron Age, this is by far the earliest clear-cut proof that the plant was consumed for its psychoactive effects, which have made it one of the most widely used drugs in the world today.If you haven’t caught our most recent ep, it’s everywhere you get your pods. We get into Joseph’s investigation into Proton’s culture of fear and the company’s massive push towards AI, and the AO3 outage and its fallout. In the section for subscribers at the Supporter level, Jason explains: We’re not tech support. (Unless you’re using the RSS trick I mentioned above.) Ready to get out of here? NASA is looking for people to live and work on the moon. And by people I mean extremely rigorously trained astronauts. "Those missions will demand technical excellence, sound judgment, teamwork, and courage," NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman in a statement released on Saturday. "NASA's astronaut corps has always called on remarkable Americans willing to take on extraordinary challenges in service to the nation." I’m staying Earthside, it’s just getting good.via Hackaday, the "music of the spheres:" Given your location, or at least an approximation of it, OrbitalWiki can determine which of the nearly 17,000 satellites it’s currently tracking are flying over you in real-time. When each satellite hits the highest point in the sky from your perspective, it will play a single note.NVIDIA is investigating its CEO, Jensen Huang, for having an affair with a suspected Chinese spy. He published on Sunday apologizing to like, everybody: “To my wife and family: I love you. I know an apology cannot undo what I have done. I hope our family will heal and that, over time, I can earn back your trust.” What makes this even more interesting is Pour one out for

item.title: Connor Hellebuyck Won’t Start In Winnipeg Because Of “Expected Win Probability”
item.author: Barry Petchesky
item.content:encoded: Some of the most memorable nights in hockey are driven by malice. If the NHL could capture in a bottle the atmosphere of John Tavares's first trip to Long Island after signing with Toronto, or Brady Tkachuk's Ottawa return as a Panther, it could and would sell it. And fans would buy it, because what these nights are really about is catharsis: the purging of resentments and the reaffirmation of loyalties. It's a nice thing to do from time to time. Builds community. Strengthens fandom. Probably good for mental health. The crowd that boos together, cheers together.Winnipeg wants and deserves a night of catharsis, to wish a not-so-fond farewell to Connor Hellebuyck, the greatest player the franchise has ever had, and who got so sick of both losing and living in Winnipeg that he forced his way to New Jersey. And wouldn't you know it, the Devils are on a Canada swing, and will take on the Jets on Tuesday. It ought to be personality-driven appointment viewing, in a league that doesn't have nearly enough of that. But the Devils have affirmed their commitment to non-entertainment. Connor Hellebuyck will not start in Winnipeg, per an all-timer of an official statement.

item.title: Star Wars Copies From the 1970s
item.author: Miss Cellania
item.content:encoded: came out in 1977, it was an immediate monster hit. Filmmakers everywhere, but especially in Italy, sat up and noticed. If the audience wants a space Western, that's what they'll get! But we had already seen space adventures for many years, so what was it about that people loved so much? A series of movies were churned out that tried to emulate as best they could, going so far as to rip off character designs and plot lines from a galaxy far, far away. The most famous of these knockoffs was an Italian film with movie stars and space battles, but not much else. Evan Puschak looks at the phenomena of low budget wannabe movies, and hones in on exactly what they were missing. Which any moviegoer who saw on a big screen in 1977 knows to be true. This video is only seven minutes long; the rest is an ad. (via kottke)

item.title: Circular Jerk
item.author: Dave Pell
item.source: NextDraft: The Day's Most Fascinating News
item.content:encoded: In 2026, there are thousands of massively scaled data centers across the world, and guys still think with their dicks. The enduring stamina of the notion that the carnal is greater than the kernel, that ramming overides the ram, and that the dong is greater than the dongle, provides yet another reminder that the key risk factors presented by the AI boom are the humans behind it (or in front of it, to the side of it, or whatever else you’re into). And thus, we found ourselves bracing for the global market response to news of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s extramarital affair. Now, the idea that a tech CEO would upload his firmware into multiple devices is hardly breaking news, but in this case, at the risk of getting too graphical, Huang installed his processing unit into the wrong hosting facility. It looks like he may have been honey-trapped by a Chinese operative. This is big news because of national security, the global AI race, and Nvidia’s technological and financial prowess—and their circular deals—that place the mega-company smack dab in the middle of the AI economy, which is smack dab in the middle of the everything economy. Nvidia’s board, which denies that any damaging spying was done, has launched an internal investigation. But what, really, can be done? “Over the past four years, Jensen Huang has become the maestro of the artificial intelligence boom and its most essential billionaire executive. Nvidia, the company he co-founded in 1993, controls an estimated 90 percent of the market for the computer chips used in the big artificial intelligence projects that are driving the U.S. economy. That dominance has made Mr. Huang one of the wealthiest people in the world, as well as an ally of President Trump.” (Gift Article): Is Jensen Huang Too Powerful to Be Punished by Nvidia? That’s another way of asking if he’s too big to fail. But this is hardly a time for braggadocio.+ Trump immediately backed Jensen Huang (Huang stands accused of simultaneous infidelity and treachery. In Trumpworld, that practically qualifies him for a Presidential Medal of Freedom). But, in a twist that will surprise no one, the Trump administration could be heavily implicated in this scandal. It turns out that some inside the administration have been worried about this issue for a while. Just not the top person. Rubio Warned Officials About Nvidia Chief’s Entanglement With Chinese Spy. “Mr. Rubio’s involvement in warning administration officials about the situation has not been previously reported. It highlights how concerns about the relationship and the spying were known to senior officials even as Mr. Huang, a pivotal figure in the explosive growth of A.I., remained an influential voice with Mr. Trump over policy on the issue.” Wait, it gets shadier. Commerce Dept. Chip Inquiry Was Halted After Nvidia Intervention. “Investigators at the Commerce Department were deep into a monthslong investigation of a Singaporean company that they suspected of smuggling Nvidia’s artificial intelligence chips into China when their work came to a sudden halt late last year.”+ So far, the tech and broader markets are holding up better than expected in light of this news. As for Nvidia, it saw about $330 billion cut from its market cap on Monday. I’m guessing most investors (and political observers) will see this as a buying opportunity.“How do you summon up shame for so many years of shamelessness? … For some, it will be impossible, even embarrassing, to keep Trump at arm’s length. Vance, for example, who long ago likened Trump to Hitler and to ‘cultural heroin,’ is far too bound to the regime, too eager for a promotion, too memorable as MAGA’s highest-ranking smirk to bow out now. The vice president can pray that the Iran war is his party’s only problem, but the guy who promoted lies about Haitian immigrants eating dogs and cats, who publicly supported fatal Immigration and Customs Enforcement raids and who defended the most reviled attack ad in the 2026 midterms might want to try that ‘honest conversation’ with himself. One day you’re riding the Trump train; the next, you find yourself tied to the tracks.” (Gift Article): JD Vance Needs to Stop Trying. (Trump’s enablers like JD Vance are political versions of Bruce Willis in . They don’t realize they’re already dead.)Even the losers get lucky sometimes. But luckily for betting apps and prediction markets, not very often. “It’s true that millions of people use them only occasionally, and only to have a bit of fun. But these people are of modest value to the companies. The least active two-thirds of licensed sportsbook gamblers account for just 2.7% of estimated revenue, according to a Bloomberg Businessweek analysis of almost 140,000 bettors across 29 states in 2024 and ’25. The more lucrative bettors are the small but growing cohort of gamblers exhibiting likely problem behavior. A classic symptom would be topping off their sportsbook account hundreds of times a year. Without these people, digital sportsbooks could lose about 60% of their revenue. That’s unlikely to happen: Of the people who place deposits into sportsbooks monthly, 1 in 5 will eventually do so daily, our analysis found.” (Gift Article): The Spiral.“Location tracking might start, for younger kids, with an AirTag slipped into a backpack, jacket, or shoe. (Skechers now makes shoes with a dedicated compartment in the sole.) For kids old enough to have their own smartwatch or phone, the GPS is built right in—and so parents keep tracking them into adolescence and even beyond. Three-quarters of parents with teenagers ages 14 to 17 had access to their kids’ location data, according to one study. Even among college students, one-third were being tracked by their parents, according to another study, conducted in 2021 by Michaeline Jensen, a psychologist at the University of North Carolina at Greensboro. Five years later, Jensen says, that number is even higher: More than half of college students are being tracked, per her unpublished data. In her own lab, she’s learned that even her graduate students continue to be tracked; she told me about one student, 29, who recently defended her dissertation but whose mom still checks—and calls about—her location.” (Gift Article): What Constant Surveillance Is Doing to Children. (I don’t have to actively track my kids’ location. They share my Uber account…)+ How much can older generations screw up the world before the youth finally take to the streets? About this much. “Their reasons for taking to the streets have varied widely, from protesting against corruption and an unequal playing field to calling for more investment in education, affordable housing and action on the climate crisis.” ‘A global political awakening’: how Gen Z protests are sweeping the world.+ The Vampire Strikes Back: America to Trump: “We couldn’t hate you more.” Trump to America: “Hold my Miller.” A Chief of Staff Who ‘Will Crack Skulls‘. “Where Wiles served as something of a guardrail—making sure Trump was fully briefed and that he understood the risks and pitfalls of any decision—Miller has played the role of an accelerant for a president who already has rash tendencies.” + “The College Football Playoff and ESPN have signed a five-year deal that will expand the field to 24 teams in 2027 with ESPN as the event’s continued broadcast partner.” This is in keeping with their usual M.O. Good for the bottom line. Bad for the game. (And I’m not just mad because even if they expand it to 124 teams, Cal still wouldn’t make it…)+ “‘Imagine explaining a wellness darty to someone who went to college in 2012,’ Aydan Child, the 25-year-old Gainesville, Fla., resident wrote in a September TikTok post that quickly went viral. In the video, fraternity brothers can be seen running shirtless and holding Pilates poses in front of the Pi Kappa Alpha house at the University of Florida. The post prompted outrage from various corners of the internet in what amounted to a generational panic; millennials and Gen Xers expressed horror at the notion that today’s college kids are hyper-fit and totally sober. The New York Post called the photos ‘bone-chilling.'” (Gift Article): Cold Plunges, Fitness Pop-Ups: The Students Pushing Clean Living on Campus. (Marlon Brando whisper-voice: “The horror, the horror.”)

item.title: Boot

item.title: The Democracy Election
item.author: 1axbxgygq0xjv9t9efsm9cfezkmplfrfffcijn@bf56x.hubspotemail.net
item.content:encoded: When voters went to the polls Tuesday, democracy was on their minds.Exit polls from the midterms show that 33% of voters named the state of democracy as the most important issue facing the country. By comparison, health care, foreign policy and crime all registered in the single digits. Only the economy ranked higher, at 39%.For Democratic voters, the results were even starker. Nearly half (47%) ranked the state of democracy as their top issue. No other issue, including the economy, came close.To paraphrase James Carville: for Democrats in 2026, it was democracy, stupid. As one prominent pollster put it to me, the new data is “consistent with our polls throughout the year, which showed that democracy was a top-tier motivator for Democrats.”Conventional wisdom holds that democracy resonates mainly with older, college-educated voters, and some strategists dismiss the issue for that reason. That’s a mistake. These voters turn out at the highest rates, donate to campaigns and follow politics closely.Most importantly, although these voters are now anti-Trump, they have not always been Democrats. In 2012, Mitt Romney won white college-educated voters, and the same group favored Republicans in the 2014 midterms.Only since Trump’s arrival on the political scene has this group become a key part of the Democratic coalition. Some are so-called Never Trump Republicans; others are swing voters who have moved toward Democrats.The bottom line: writing off democracy as an issue because it appeals to older, educated voters would be a serious error. Democrats do not have a lock on this cohort, and democracy is the issue that currently binds them most closely to a big-tent party with many other constituencies.Then there are Black voters, who watched as the Supreme Court gutted what remained of the Voting Rights Act’s protections in . Republicans believed the decision would pave the way for replacing Black elected officials throughout the South. It had the opposite effect.Black voters, the Democratic Party’s most reliable constituency, turned out in record numbers to prove that a conservative Supreme Court will not strip democracy and the right to vote from their community. If that isn’t pro-democracy action, nothing is.Those who argue that economic issues weighed more heavily than democracy also need to explain why two of the most effective ad campaigns across the states focused on Trump’s refusal to fully release the Epstein files and the GOP’s support for data centers.Neither fits neatly into an economic frame. Both, however, fit squarely within the set of issues that make up the pro-democracy cause.The federal government’s failure to fully release the Epstein files was an easily understood example of an administration refusing to abide by the rule of law. The Justice Department’s complicity in withholding them angered those concerned with the separation of powers and constitutional limits on presidential power.Opposition to data centers is likewise driven, at least in part, by a concern that wealthy Trump supporters are receiving preferential treatment while local communities are ignored. While some argue that this reflects a separate concern about corruption, I think that defines democracy too narrowly.When people express concern about the state of democracy, they are not referring only to elections but to whether the consent of the governed still has meaning. Elections are central to democracy, but so are the rule of law and accountability for those who break it.Trump’s attacks on our elections obviously made voters concerned about our democracy. But because he carried these attacks out by abusing the power of the federal government, the issue became broader than typical Republican voter suppression.For the new majorities in Congress and Democratic state officials, taking the democracy issue seriously means more than paying lip service to the dozen or so pro-voting bills that are regularly discussed. They should think more boldly and expansively about how to protect democracy from the threats of the modern era.Candidates considering a run for president or other office in 2028 must understand that democracy is the single most important issue for Democratic primary voters, and act accordingly. That means prioritizing it in their campaigns rather than treating it as a secondary concern.The fate of democracy in the Trump era is the central issue of our generation. The 2026 midterms bore that out, and I expect 2028 will make it even more obvious.The question is whether Democratic campaigns and officeholders will accept this or keep trying to explain it away in favor of traditional messaging.For the sake of the party and the country, I hope they choose the former. It is our job to make sure they do.

item.title: Maxime Denuc
item.author: Flow State
item.content:encoded: Today we’re listening to Maxime Denuc, a French electronic musician based in Brussels. He grew up in the French countryside playing piano, and got into composition as a teenager.He studied theory of art and language at EHESS Paris and pursued a PhD in musicology. His latest record, , is made up of compositions for a MIDI-controlled pipe organ at St. Antonius Church in Düsseldorf. The historic instrument was programmed to play minimalist and trance-like loops which reverberate across the cathedral’s interior. We’re also playing from 2022, which was recorded the same way, producing “acoustic dance music” by controlling the organ’s keyboards, stops, and pedals.We wish you a great start to your week.

item.title: Hide your slop PR descriptions behind <details><summary>
item.author: Simon Willison
item.content:encoded: Most of the changes I make to my projects these days come in the form of PRs opened for me by Claude Code or Codex. The PR is my unit of work - I use them to bundle commits together, iterating on them until a feature is complete, document decisions and then merge the finished result. Today's coding agents are great at writing PR descriptions.They're too good at describing the workThe problem is that they are good. An agent-written PR description is accurate and comprehensive. It describes the problem, the detailed solution, and the steps taken to verify it. That's a lot of information to absorb.It's not necessarily slop, but it like slop!It's very easy to spot an AI-written PR, and as with other forms of AI writing my instant reaction is best summarized as "I'm not reading all of that". It doesn't matter how accurate or useful the information is, I'm instantly put off by the thought that it will take me longer to read than it took the driving author to write... even when that driving author is me!I want human editorial judgement. I want someone to have thought just long enough about the PR to give me a human-approved introduction that helps me understand, at a high level, what the PR is for and whether it deserves more of my attention.I think I've found a low-effort way to do this that feels right.Hide most of it in a details/summaryThe HTML elements render as a collapsed heading (the summary) that can be expanded to view the larger piece of text. The code looks like this:Claude Opus 5.5The hook Plugins implement register_agent_reference_types(datasette)... Crucially, is supported in GitHub Markdown. You can drop those tags directly into an issue comment or PR description and GitHub will hide the details and display just the summary plus an expansion arrow.I've started using this for my AI-generated pull requests.The opening paragraph of my PRs will be carefully selected to act as a high-level explanation of what's going on - the shortest text a human can read that will help get them up to speed.I'll sometimes throw in a screenshot as well, since images are often the best way to quickly illustrate a new feature.The full agent-written essay then follows in a . I use the model name and often the effort level as that summary, to make it abundantly clear what is going on - "Claude Opus 5.5 Medium" for example.My PRs don't feel nearly as sloppy now! The information is all still there, but a reader can glance at it and get the top, human-curated information without their eyes glazing over at multiple paragraphs of agent-written details.I don't always write the introduction myself - sometimes the agent has given me what I need already, hidden away in the avalanche of other text. My promise to the reader is that the short opener will represent my human judgement as to what is definitely worth their time.Here are some recent examples where I've used this pattern, including the opener I used:I used to have trouble remembering the order of the tags - is it or ?Here are two tricks that helped me.First, and most obviously, the is clearly the bit where you summarize the details. That's the tag for your line of text that can be clicked to expand - the element must then wrap everything else.An even better trick is to always refer to these two tags as "details-summary"."details-summary" is two syllables followed by three syllables. That rolls off the tongue more smoothly than the three-two punch of "summary-details".Say "details-summary" out loud just a few times and you'll never forget the order of the tags again.(I still wish GitHub would add a button to their Markdown editor for this - partly to save me painstakingly typing it on my mobile keyboard, and partly to help spread the word to more GitHub users that this feature exists.)

item.title: Yak-Shaving Overload
item.author: Ernie Smith
item.source: Tedium: The Dull Side of the Internet.
item.content:encoded: Over the years I’ve gotten myself into all varieties of technical rabbit holes and wild goose chases. But I’m feeling weird about my latest trip, involving a forgotten Linux tablet. I blame AI.Recently, I took on a project that I thought would be a lot of fun … but in the end, I did not like how it made me feel. And I think it reflects the real dangers of leaning too aggressively on AI for stuff you’d like to try out.A quick explainer: About four years ago, I got a hold of a JingPad, a Linux-based tablet with a massive Achilles’ heel. The problem? It was sold as a Linux-first tablet on ARM, but it was built around an SoC that was not actually particularly open. The Unisoc Tiger T510, as I’ve written, was built for Android, and it has PowerVR graphics that didn’t have an open-source driver. Worse, the company that made it disappeared off the face of the Earth just a handful of months after it first appeared.The JingPad was a working, fully functional tablet that had been done dirty by its ownership and a bad engineering decision. It was a perfect candidate for the very kind of deconstruction project that has been taking the internet by storm in recent weeks.So, my goal was this: Let’s see if I can use Claude, Deepseek, Xiaomi MiMo, and other LLMs to get this dang thing working in a modern version of Linux. Certain components, namely the proprietary GPU, might prove difficult, but using Ghidra, Reverse Engineer Anything (REA), and a willing-to-go-at-it LLM, it could take things down the road for me.The good, and bad, of an insane yak-shaving projectThis is an example of yak-shaving, a concept in which one project gradually evolves into numerous complex branches that never seem to end. For those not familiar, it is based on a skit called “Yak Shaving Day,” which I’ve helpfully embedded above.Tech projects have a tendency to devolve into wild goose chases like this, as hinted above, but this was a whole new beast to me.Anyway, I want to make clear that this project wasn’t an outright failure. From literally nothing but an empty boot screen, we got the device to load a relatively modern version of Fedora on a “dirty” Linux kernel, based on 6.18. In many ways, it worked, complete with a working touchscreen screen, a charging battery, WiFi access, and an accessible GNOME interface. While not especially fast, I believe it is about as stable as JingOS, the software that came on it in 2022 and itself did not have GPU accelerated graphics.There were even fun quirks that emerged as I was working on this. I got the flashlight for the camera working on the back, even though there’s literally no use case where it’d actually be useful. And I made significant progress adding FM radio support for the device, despite the fact that, like most mobile devices, FM radio support was never an actual feature of the tool. (In both cases, I thought it would be funny, even though the joke was honestly limited to just me.)Unfortunately, getting to this point created a project that I would best describe as all-consuming. I had a swarm of different agents going at different components, different parts of the device, attempting to scrape details from old firmware versions and related projects in the hope that it’d uncover something missed previously. The result: I had to baby the damn thing all day, managing a bunch of LLMs and rebooting the device as the agents I was using went down one dead-end after another. And shockingly, the thing that kind of made the process less fun and more of a quagmire? It wasn’t the GPU, as I expected; it was the sound.I got as far as having all the components of the sound card separately working; the DMA chip, the speakers, the codecs, and so on. The GNOME settings app even recognized that the sound card was there. But after receiving something like 50 “this is the last thing before you finally hear sound” messages from DeepSeek, I realized that I had gotten my own brain into a dangerous loop. It was nonstop dopamine hit on top of nonstop dopamine hit—the promise of instant gratification without getting gratified—and after a while, I kind of just felt mentally drained by it all.This was a “me” project, one that I wanted to see in the world, but in the end it was kind of getting in the way of me thinking about literally anything else.The way I broke the chain, at least for now, was simple: I put the tablet away for now. I’m going to try my best to get a healthy distance from it. If and when I come back to this project, I want to ensure I’m doing it for reasons that help me learn something rather than stress me out.In the right context, things like this can be goodThis all sounds like a dangerous hobby. But to make the counterargument: For years, we’ve heard stories about smart devices and other objects losing support over time because a company shut down a server somewhere, or chose not to modernize them. With moves like these, we can revive these devices.For example, the seemingly dead Hackintosh scene has actually seen signs of life, thanks to AI. There’s now a driver for modern-day Nvidia cards on Intel Hackintoshes. It is now possible to boot MacOS on a Snapdragon PC. And Cutefish, a new MacOS-like distro, has promised something previously thought impossible—working graphical MacOS apps in a Linux environment.A decade ago, when Hackintosh was hitting its peak point in popularity, all this stuff was crazy talk. No way was this going to happen.And to be clear, there have been other projects I’ve tried that went way better than the one above. As I recently wrote in Boxed News, I was able to turn Dux Shell (formerly Dank Material Shell) into a usable TV computing experience.Yes, AI is capable of reshaping computing experiences in new ways, in ways that some might find culturally frustrating if the reason you get into tech is because of specific scenes. (I personally don’t, and think the line between cool stuff and gatekeeping is quite small.)But I’m personally of the view that in cases like the JingPad, where this tablet would be sitting around being useless otherwise, stuff like REA could have genuine value. After all, even if I don’t end up using it to type the next Great American blog post, it can still be useful as a makeshift self-hosting device or even just a lightweight way to surf the web. And I’m hopeful that, eventually, I’ll turn this into a feature-complete device, even with the components that Unisoc and Imagination didn’t bother to make public. However …Shave yaks? If you value your mental health, pace yourselfIf there’s anything I’ve learned about myself over the past decade, I get sucked into different directions way too easily. I can get obsessed with things, and that obsession can sometimes lead to cool places. (See &udm=14.)But something about the process of attempting to use AI to fix an old tablet felt kind of damaging to a routine in a way that few of my hobbies have over the years. I mentioned Hackintoshing before, and honestly that’s kind of what it reminds me of the most, this attempt to make something do a thing it was never meant to do. But when so much of what you’re doing is working up against something hyping up every action, it’s hard not to feel hollow at the end of it.As is highlighted by the fact that I publish a little less often these days, I don’t use AI for any of my actual writing. I try taking my time with it. But in a world where it seems like AI is the decorative bird of technology, it can intrude in dangerous ways, with costs that don’t necessarily show themselves right away. And I’m not talking about tokens.I’m a well-known yak shaver. It’s what I do. This newsletter is a shrine to yak-shaving at the end of the day. But I did not like the way I felt at the end of this week, having hit the reset button on the JingPad for the 250th time. I’m sure I’m not alone here.My suggestion to anyone else who yak-shaves: Approach agents with caution. After all, an AI agent does not have a limit; you do. Projects like these only take and take your energy, and leave you with a broken-feeling brain.And unlike a static code window or a page of docs, an agent can make false claims or hype up promises it can’t back up.Last week was utterly packed with election stuff, which I’ll let you find yourself. But one story you may have missed last week was the death of Salon, one of the digital journalism OGs. Important website that deserved better than an unceremonial shutdown out of nowhere. I’m going to write more about this soon, I think.I’m sure you haven’t asked yourself what the guy from the “Pretty Fly (for a White Guy)” video has been up to for the past 28 years. But in case you had a poser-shaped hole in your brain, here’s the answer. Fun fact: He appears on stage at shows for The Offspring sometimes.
