item.title: parse_number() as a SQLite extension: C vs Rust
item.author: Simon Willison
item.content:encoded: I was out walking the dog when I got curious about how easy/difficult it would be to write a SQLite C extension that adds a function for turning strings like or into numeric values that could be summed and sorted.I'm thinking about a SQLite custom function 'parse_number(value)' that strips ',', '$', '£' and '%', handles a leading '-', and returns 'NULL' for anything it can’t parseExplore the difference between building this as a SQLite extension in C v.s. in Rust - I want to compare performance and code complexity and size of the resulting.soThis gave me a solid starting point - the Rust extension was 321 KB (using Rusqlite) and 298 KB (using sqlite-loadable-rs), while the C extension was 14 KB. But the Rust extension was faster!Turns out that's because the Rust equivalent of C's is "twice as fast". So I prompted:Try writing your own C function for parsing text into a decimal number that catches up to or beats the Rust implementationAnd it did, using "Clinger's fast path":Net cost per row over 2 million rows, lower is better:Finally, I had it rewrite the prototype as a research report to match the others in simonw/research by prompting this:Clone simonw/research from GitHub and turn your above investigation into a research report as seen in that repository - you can give me a zip file to download that contains your new folder

item.title: Unc: Here for It, #367
item.author: SRS0=4gOt=I5=m.ghost.io=bounce+3cffae.7bdc18-misc=muneer.top@eforward.registrar-servers.com
item.content:encoded: Hi! It's R. Eric Thomas. From the internet?Hi!What y'all know about wearing orthopedic shoes at the clurb?!What y'all know about dropping it low but keeping your arch support high, okay?!What y'all know about breaking a sweat but not your ankle, huh?!This all started very innocently. I was out with some folks and it got to be around midnight and but one member of the group is like a divining rod for a good time and she wasn't done. One minute, I was idling on the sidewalk, casually observing her checking Uber and the next minute I was being extraordinarily renditioned into the back of a black van.Now, I love all my little British spy shows--Black Doves, Slow Horses, The Night Manager, The Day Manager, The Middle Manager--so I'm prepared for this kind of thing to happen. But when we arrived at the club, a dive-y longstanding Philly dance bar called The Dolphin (also the name of a British spy show), I realized I was in trouble.I dress fairly cool, but I am under no delusion. I am unc. I'm not pressed about this. I, in fact, have nieces and nephews! But unc does not belong in the clurb!First of all, I was wearing a trench coat I got in Italy (yes, that could be a brag, but also sometimes the truth sounds impressive. I can't help it! I'm addicted to honesty! Selectively! When it serves me!)I was also wearing the most god-awful ugly chunky orthotic shoes you've ever seen in your life. But my friend paid my cover at the club (a reverse ransom!), so in I went.Let me explain the shoes. You see, my feet hurt because I be running around in your mind all day. I don't really need to go into the physiology of it, but I realized last year that a lot of the body discomfort I was feeling was because all my shoes, except my Birks, are cute but ultimately functionless. I am also cute but ultimately functionless, so who is driving the bus?I looked into footwear options that weren't going to give "Obama on the campaign trail" or "running the marathon this morning" and I found this company, Vionic, that makes a wide variety of shoes, including the aforementioned absolutely hideous, incredibly comfortable white sneaker.[I originally put a picture of it here but I had to remove it because, out of context, it will absolutely impact your impression of me as a cool, beautiful person.]The thing is: a hideous, chunky shoe is exactly what Gen Z and Gen Alpha are wearing nowadays. Everyone's wearing these huge pants and something that looks like home insulation on their feet and either a crop top or a one of those parachutes from a kid's birthday party at a soft surfaces gym. No in-between.I could the youths into thinking I am by wearing these big ass sneakers. And no one would know that these particular ugly shoes are Pop-Pop 3000s and not whatever it is they're wearing.Now, I used to go to the Dolphin all the time back in the day, the day being Obama-era America, which, chronologically and emotionally, was 1,000 years ago. When I used to go, my favorite night was a throwback night where they played remixes of Motown songs.Last night was also a throwback night... to 1999.Specifically, they were spinning hip hop from 1999 and the early 2000s, aka the exact music I was throwing it down to when I first started going to the clurb. What's worse, every single person in the packed club except our group when these songs that I knew every word to came out.But who cares! I'm up in the clurb in my Meemah Supremes and feeling My goodness gracious, do I love a shenanigan. I wasn't there at the clurb to meet anyone or to do anything but bump it to Eve and Mary J. Blige and Lil Kim and Fat Joe and other people who have since been cancelled. I love to dance and you don't have to be under a particular age to be allowed to do it and with my stealthy, fugly shoes, there were no consequences beyond my pride and, honey, who needs that?When I went to start this post, I was looking for images to go along with it and I googled "old guy at the club" and this is the first link that popped up.Obviously, I clicked on it, wondering what these 70- and 80-year-olds had to say for themselves.Beloved, almost every person they interviewed in this article was my exact current age.You know what, though, good for them. It's a privilege to get older. It's a privilege to go out and experience life. It's a privilege to hear songs that you actually recognize on the dance floor. (Call me when they start blasting Celine Dion at the clurb, honey. I'll be out breaking it down in my Mall Walker X's) If it's unc behavior to dance it out, enjoy myself, and then wake up the next morning feeling great, then unc I shall be!up in the clurb in my Meemah Supremes and feeling ,Eric

item.title: What Cornell says about universities’ MAGA complicity
item.content:encoded: In the wake of a national story of an alleged gang rape at the The whole debacle has refreshed interest in the previous big controversy of Kotikoff’s brief but eventful presidential tenure: Cornell’s $60 million settlement with Donald Trump’s administration, which was announced in November 2025. The agreement was widely lambasted as a capitulation to the White House’s all-out war on diversity, equity and inclusion programs. Not only did the university implicitly concede that programs meant to help women and minorities are discriminatory against white men, they agreed to hand over data on race in admissions to the Trump administration and impose anti-DEI materials, provided by the White House, on faculty and staff. After the settlement was announced, the American Association of University Professors said in a statement that the agreement would “threaten some of the most vulnerable students on campus and invite ongoing federal government supervision to reduce the diversity of Cornell’s student body.” In July, the organization published an extensive report comparing the administration’s war on DEI to the Red Scare of the 1950s and called on university leadership to resist the Trump administration’s efforts to destroy racial diversity and gender equity efforts on campus. As the AAUP report shows, Cornell was far from the only university to cave to Trump; the norm for colleges and universities was rapid compliance. Diversity offices were shut down. Progressive student protesters were bullied and punished. Title IX protections, including rules protecting students from sexual harassment and abuse, were scaled back. Anecdotes have spread from faculty and students about a new chill descending over college campuses — a fear of retaliation for acknowledging the ongoing realities of racism, sexism and homophobia on campuses and in larger society. The fallout from the Cornell assault accusations, however, suggests that it may have been more than fear that was compelling this swift bending of the knee by many universities to Trump. There is also a degree of complicity. Progressive reforms to make campuses more welcoming to women and minority students are often a hassle for university administrators, even those ideologically who are aligned with the left. It means conflicts with board members, donors and alumni with more conservative leanings. It means having to handle student complaints of harassment, discrimination and even sexual abuse that would be easier to sweep under the rug. It means having to confront institutions — like fraternities — that reinscribe racism and sexism but are often simultaneously protected by the most elite and wealthy people connected to the universities. Giving into the Trump administration on DEI means being able to revert to older, easier ways of doing things — even if it comes at the expense of student freedom and safety. It’s worth remembering that Jane Doe filed her complaint before Trump was president. Her case has all the hallmarks of an institution that tried to make her go away. Cornell police excluded relevant language — including the unambiguous phrase “I was raped” — from their report to the district attorney on Doe’s statement. Her lawyer claims that the university made her believe that the authorities were pursuing a criminal investigation, even though her case had already been closed. As Cornell philosophy professor Kate Manne noted in an essay for New York magazine, the university’s student code of conduct has a stricter definition of rape-by-intoxication than New York State’s, which would seem to cover the situation alleged here, where a woman is as high and drunk as Doe admits she was. And yet only five of the seven men accused were expelled from school, even as she was forced to drop out due to the subsequent stress and anxiety. If Cornell is guilty of abandoning Jane Doe, it has no reason to fear consequences from the federal government for failure to enforce Title IX protections against sexual abuse on campus.If Cornell is guilty of abandoning Jane Doe, it has no reason to fear consequences from the federal government for failure to enforce Title IX protections against sexual abuse on campus. As the New York Times reported this week, the Trump administration barely enforced the law during his first term. In his second term, enforcement is basically nonexistent. According to analysis by the Washington Post, Cornell’s track record is already alarming. From 2018 to 2024, there were 1,216 reports of sexual assault, domestic and dating violence, and stalking on campus. Only 51 people were ever found responsible, and of those, fewer than half faced serious consequences.Jane Doe reported her alleged rape a few days after Trump got elected. With that history in mind, Cornell police and administrators could have had every reason to believe there would be no federal repercussions if they failed to reach a just outcome in her case.Jane Doe’s lawyer, Thomas Giuffra, told CNN that his client “was not somebody who was a legacy [student], from a wealthy family” and “came from a small town.” Fraternities, in stark contrast, enjoy immense protections from exactly those wealthy people from legacy families. As historian Nick Syrett, author of “The Company He Keeps: A History of White College Fraternities,” told Time, former fraternity members are “a base of alumni that universities don’t want to upset because they’re generous and they’re powerful.” Whatever an administrator’s personal feelings, in a situation like this, it is objectively easier to cut loose an alleged victim rather than take on alleged assailants who are well-connected to powerful elites.From a purely self-interested point of view, the Trump administration’s demands that schools give up policies and programs to help women and minority students is a win-win for administrators. It allows school leaders to give up a miserable, uphill battle against elite forces, while handing them a way to deflect blame onto the White House for forcing them into it.We can’t peer into the hearts of administrators and know the exact mix of complicity and fear that drove these capitulations. But the Cornell case is a stark illustration of why the prospect of letting Trump have what he wants has a dark allure.

item.title: You Could Be County Clerk, Or Sheriff!
item.author: Chris Thompson
item.content:encoded: You—yes, you—could be in elected office today. The median Defector reader is a smart and good-looking progressive with impeccable taste. What other qualifications do you really need? Had you thrown your hat in ahead of the blue wave, today you could be your state's lieutenant governor. Hell, for that matter, maybe you your state's lieutenant governor. Have you checked your mail?Consider the case of Sebastian Matta, a 19-year-old sophomore at Arizona State University. He has a 3.25 GPA, per the , and he lives at home with his parents. Starting in February, Matta will be the Superior Court Clerk of Maricopa County, which has a geographic area larger than New Jersey and a population larger than Oregon. Matta will lead a department that, according to Phoenix-area CBS affiliate KTVK, processes more than 16,000 documents per day and has an annual budget of $65 million. Matta will be the boss to some 670 veteran professional staff."I hope that they realize that I’m just not any 19-year-old," said Matta, hoping to give confidence to the hundreds of people who will soon be working under him in an incredibly complex bureaucracy.

item.content:encoded: Virginia restores voting rights for those previously incarceratedVirginians voted 56% to 43% to end a lifetime voting ban for people with felony convictions, a practice that dates back to 1902. Data shows the ban kept about 1 in 10 Black Virginians from voting. Reason >Missouri throws out its new congressional mapSixty-two percent of voters rejected a map that lawmakers had redrawn in the middle of the decade. They also passed Amendment 6, which makes it harder for lawmakers to undo laws passed by popular vote. State Court Report >Abortion rights hold in three statesVoters in Virginia and Nevada protected abortion rights in the midterm elections. In Missouri, voters said no to repealing the abortion rights amendment they passed in 2024. State Court Report >California funds affordable housing and schoolsVoters approved an $11.25 billion housing bond for lower-income renters and people who are unhoused. They also voted for a permanent tax on people earning over $360,000 to fund local schools. CalMatters >Towns across 10 states vote down data centersIn about 40 local measures, most voters rejected new data centers in their towns. Data centers are more likely to be built in communities of color. Nearly 80% of voters in Joliet, Illinois, where Black and Latino residents have fought pollution for years, voted against them. Capital B >Massachusetts passes same-day voter registrationThanks to voters, people in Massachusetts can now register and vote on the same day. Voters in California and Colorado also rejected stricter voter ID and mail ballot rules. State Court Report >Arizona says no to anti-DEIArizona voters rejected limits on DEI programs by a large margin, turning the tide against hateful rhetoric. State Court Report >Colorado says no to police reporting immigration statusColorado rejected a measure that would have made police report people’s immigration status to federal officials. The result is still pending. State Court Report >Vermont adds equal protection and the right to organizeVoters in Vermont passed two amendments: one adds equal protection to the state constitution, and the other protects workers’ right to organize. Both give people stronger legal ground against unfair treatment at work. State Court Report >

item.title: Senile old shitwit gets his Dana Whites mixed up. Where the fuck is the press?
item.author: Jeff Tiedrich
item.source: everyone is entitled to my own opinion
item.content:encoded: You know, I’m so old that I can remember all the way back to , when The New York Times finally published an article confirming what we all already knew: that Dear Leader is bugfuck nuts. It was a well-researched piece, with numerous examples of Donny barking out incoherent nonsense as his pudding-brain visibly leaked out of his ears. I have a question. Whatever happened to that story? It barely made a ripple in the national zeitgeist. No other news outlet picked it up. Even the Times dropped it after one day.Shouldn’t a well-documented account of a sitting president whose brain has gone I am pleased to announce that the Great Dana White, a violent Fighter and Warrior, has been offered the job of Press Secretary of the United States. I have requested that he bring with him assistants, even though some are not from our Country, of Islam Makhachev, Khabib Nurmagomedov, Justin Gaethje, Daniel Cormier, Amanda Nunes, and Kayla Harris. We need these people to defend us against the Lunatic Left. Dana will be a Press Secretary like none other. Dana, please take the job! President DONALD J. TRUMPWhat the fuck even is this? Can we not all simply agree to agree that offering the job of White House PressSec to some jamoke who hosts cage matches is just flat out deranged?Look at that. Article after article, reacting to the putrid mouth-farts of a lunatic as if they were worthy of serious analysis. Donny, for the umpteenth time, shits out something completely insane, and the press dutifully writes it all up, as if Dear Leader were masterfully playing some kind of nth-dimensional chess that we peons are all just too stupid to comprehend.Which — and I cannot put too fine a point on this — he isn’t. He isn’t playing any kind of chess at all. He’s wandering, lost and confused, with both horsies shoved up his nostrils.What are we doing here, media? Will nobody point out the obvious, that the emperor has no brain?A friend whom I will credit when he gives me permission offers the following conjecture about the insane public attempt to hire UFC dude Dana White as WH Press Secretary:“I think the real story is that someone suggested a woman named Dana White (who has publicist credentials via Fox and Heritage) and Trump misunderstood.”Her bio is below, also via my friend. I think he may be right.That’s got to be it, right? It turns out there are two Dana Whites. One of them is a trained media professional who has already held a press position within the federal government. The other arranges human cockfights for money.You just know that someone in the White House said to Donny, ‘hey, why don’t we hire Dana White as PressSec’ — and the stupid fuck’s rotting brain got confused and dredged up the wrong one.That’s why, when someone said ‘hey, let’s hire Dana White,’ Donny got it wrong.What fucking insanity is this?White said Saturday that he plans to meet with Trump on Monday at the White House.Why? Dana White is not qualified to be Press Secretary. Dana White does not want to Press Secretary. So why is he flying all the way to Washington to waste an afternoon doing some Oval Bordello dog-and-pony show?Because he wants to do his crony Donny a solid. He’s willing to burn an entire day play-acting so that nobody in the White House has to confess that Dear Leader done fucked up. And the press is entirely willing to play along.The universe is just fucking with us right now.It was all about how, during the run-up to the 2024 election, the press had worked overtime to scrub all the crazy out of Donny’s campaign speeches, helping to hide his cognitive decline from the voters.It was also about about how, now that Donny had been reelected, the media was trying to sell us on the ridiculous idea that hey, maybe the second term of a fucked-up fascist might actually turn out to be a thing, if we all click our heels together three times and wish really hard. Here’s one fragment from that post of mine.the New York Times can fuck all the way off.what kind of magical, thinking is this? did Ezra Klein and Ross Douthat both experience some kind of recent head trauma that has caused them to forget the years 2017 through 2020? Donny’s first presidency was a dumpster fire of corruption, mismanagement and mass death — but somehow now, given a second chance to fuck shit up worse, Donny’s going to bring us an “American renewal”?Two years after I wrote that, the press is still treating Donny — who has grown so much more cognitively collapsed — as if he were kind of some rational actor.Keep that piece co-written by Ross Douthat in your mind, because if you had been sitting around with a bunch of friends, let’s say fifteen years ago, and someone had asked, as a goof, ‘what’s the worst possible version of 60 Minutes that you could imagine,’ you could have legitimately answered, ‘oh, I don’t know, how about that dumbfuck columnist Ross Douthat interviewing a racist game show host who somehow became president?In an interview airing Sunday on 60 Minutes, correspondent Ross Douthat asks President Trump: If it took six months of not insulting the Democrats to get a deal done, do you think you could do it?Oh look — it’s just the worst possible version of a once-respected news program, arranging for the worst possible version of a journalist to interview the worst possible version of a president, asking inane questions that would have been unthinkable, a decade an a half ago.These are not serious people, yet we’re expected to take them seriously.We pretty much a Hero of the Day after that, don’t we? “How does it feel being a loser, Mr. President?”Yes! That’s how it’s fucking done.Can we get this guy some kind of Pulitzer?Hey — it’s time for some Daily Claudia.Here’s Ms Spouse deciding what to have for lunch at the Windjammer Surf Bar in Westerly, Rhode Island, on September 10, 2024.I love this place. Look at it, it sits right next to the Atlantic Ocean.And here’s some random selfie action from June 4, 2022.Have a great Sunday, everyone.here’s your daily reminder that I can be found on Blue Sky at this link.this is going to be my closing message for the foreseeable future: do what you need to do to keep sane. if that means you need to disengage with my daily posts for a while, I get it. this community of ours will still be here when you return.to all the people who have signed on in the days since the election, . settle in as we all try to deal with the shitfuckery that’s ahead of us.we are all in this together, and we are all here for each other.

item.content:encoded: The Royals have made a couple of additions to their non-playing staff. First up: They announced the final coach of their major league hitting lab. It's local guy Hunter Mense, who is officially a hitting coach. He will join a staff that includes Connor Dawson as offensive coordinator and Marcus Thames as a hitting coach.Mense arrives in Kansas City after major league stops in Toronto and San Francisco. A local guy, he grew up in Liberty and went to school at the University of Missouri. Missouri is also where he began his coaching career. He was an assistant coach from 2011 to 2016 and was their hitting coach in 2015 and 2016.Mense then moved on to the professional ranks and was the assistant hitting coach for the Jays from 2022 to 2025, a time which culminated in their run to the World Series. Working with Toronto’s hitting coach David Popkins, he was originally tabbed to work on swing mechanics and drill design. The 2025 Blue Jays led the majors in batting average (.265), on base percentage (.333) and contact rate (78.5%). They also posted the lowest strikeout rate in the majors at 17.8 percent.He was brought to San Francisco for 2026 as part of first-year manager Tony Vitello’s staff. Their connection goes back to Mense’s playing days at Missouri. He didn’t have as much to work with in San Francisco as he did in Toronto. Several key Giants got off to a slow start offensively (gee, that sounds familiar!), and there were fingers pointed in Mense’s direction (again, familiar!). They did turn things around as guys like Rafael Devers, Bryce Eldridge and Drew Gilbert all had productive second halves of the year to varying degrees.He spoke to David Laurilla at FanGraphs back in 2022 about how he focused on improving decisions at the plate and what that did to a plate appearance."You’ve always heard about the professionalism of the at-bats, and that’s what you see here (in Toronto). Guys aren’t anxious to swing at every single pitch, because they know that 1) the stuff up here is really good, and 2) they have confidence to hit in every sort of count, in any situation, so they’re willing to take a pitch if it’s not one that they want to drive. They’re willing to wait, wait, wait, wait until they get the pitch they want. What that filters down to is the swing-decision aspect of hitting."Decision-making is so key at this level, in part because, again, the stuff is so good. They can expose you so fast, especially if you’re not a good decision-maker. They will find holes really, really fast, and are going to keep exploiting them. If you keep making bad decisions, they’re going to keep going there and expose you."I'm going to pause right there and say this feels like a fantastic hire for the organization. How many times did it seem like we were watching a hitter over the last couple of years who was just up there hacking? This isn't about what the broadcast loves to harp on in things like "a 75 percent swing" or giving kudos for going the opposite way to move a runner. It's about having a plan to find that pitch you can do damage on. That may be about going the opposite way, which is fine. But again...it's about having a plan and finding the right pitch.“The one thing that we have to make sure of as coaches, and as an organization, is that when you’re teaching swing decisions, it’s not about taking the balls. It’s about being aggressive on the pitches you want to hit. I think that’s how good coaches teach it. They give guys the freedom to swing at every single pitch that’s in the zone where they can drive the ball. They’re working in areas where they can hit home runs and produce extra-base hits.“A good decision is just as much swinging at the pitch that you can drive as it is taking the breaking ball that’s out of the zone. Both weigh heavily, and you could even say that swinging at a pitch that you should drive out of the yard is more important. One will get you deeper in the count and might get you a walk. The other one is going to give you a run if you square it up.”How about that? Make the right swing decisions and you can find a pitch you can rip. So simple, yet kind of complex. I'm excited to see what Mense can do with the hitters on this club.As Speier recounts in his story, LeVangie has been a part of just about every aspect of the Red Sox organization during his time with the team. He was an advance scout for the Sox from 2006 to 2012 and was given credit for preparation work that culminated in Boston's 2007 World Series title. He then moved to the major league staff, first as a bullpen coach (2013-2019, picking up another ring in '13) and then as a pitching coach in 2018 and 2019. When the Red Sox won a title in 2018, pitcher Rick Porcello called LeVangie "the heart and soul of our staff." LeVangie shifted over to the pro scouting staff after the 2019 season.LeVangie's role with the Red Sox exceeded that of a conventional bullpen coach. Almost any adjustment made by a Boston pitcher in recent years came with some input from LeVangie. He's the one who suggested that Drew Pomeranz switch sides of the rubber — right before Pomeranz submitted the best prolonged stretch of his career. He's the one who was on top of Craig Kimbrel all last season, making sure he kept his mechanics in order. He's the one who back in 2016 helped straighten out Clay Buchholz during his stints in the bullpen.In fact, if there's one caveat to LeVangie's promotion, one complaint emerging from Boston pitchers, it's this one, from Kimbrel: "I'm going to miss hanging out with him in the bullpen. … He has a game plan every day and understands each guy. As a pitching coach, that’s the number-one thing: understanding everyone has something different and how to work with that."The story also included praise for LeVangie from guys like Chris Sale and Pedro Martinez. Seems like a couple of good guys to vouch for your pitching bona fides. No clue what's going on in Boston as they've had something of a brain drain from their front office and field staff over the last couple of seasons. It's wild that someone who has spent over 35 years in an organization in various capacities, how is massively respected, would just pick up and move on. Sure feels like the Red Sox's loss is the Royals gain. The annual GM meetings open this week in Las Vegas. The buzzword around this yearly confab is “groundwork.” As in, there are never any expectations around this gathering when it comes to moves and signings, but its where the genesis of such deals take shape. There is a slightly different tilt to this year’s edition, given commissioner Rob Manfred and his lockout lust.Will moves come together quicker than usual? Will this be the week that free agents start to migrate to new clubs? Difficult to tell, but you know what they say about old habits. The current crop of general managers give off a cautious vibe (although there are certainly some exceptions). Given the amount of groundwork (there’s that buzzword!) often necessary to pull off anything these days, I sort of doubt anything seismic develops. The acceleration that everyone is predicting when it comes to the free agent frenzy will come probably in the last week of November.The Silver Slugger finalists were announced this week. Like with the Gold Gloves earlier, there is a solid Royals contingent among the potential winners.Bobby Witt Jr. is seeking his third consecutive Silver Slugger at shortstop. I would like to think he’s a shoo-in, but there’s going to be some competition from Detroit’s Kevin McGonigle. McGonigle, who split time between second and short finished ahead of Witt in OBP (.376 to .359), but Witt came out ahead in slugging percentage (.441 to .430). It could swing either way, but I’d bet on McGonigle given he’s pulling up to this honor as the presumptive AL Rookie of the Year. Congrats to the other shortstop finalist Zach Neto of the Angels on his third-place finish.At catcher, Carter Jensen is a finalist with Detroit’s Dillon Dingler. Feels like there are some good bats up the middle in the AL Central. I make Jensen to be the favorite given he topped Dingler in just about every offensive metric you can pull up. If Jensen does in fact win the award, he will be the sixth rookie catcher to do so. The others? Benito Santiago and Matt Nokes in 1987, Craig Biggio in 1989 and Mike Piazza in 1993. Nice company.The Royals third finalist is Jac Caglianone. A year ago, did you think we would be talking about Cags being up for any award, let alone this one? While I always believed he would turn things around, I couldn’t say I was expecting anything like what we saw last summer. Caglianone is up against Wilyer Abreu, Randy Arozarena, Cody Bellinger, Cahse DeLauter, Riley Greene, Tristian Peters and Mike Trout. Caglianone’s .494 slugging percentage does top the list of finalists so it’s not like he’s an outsider. I think he has a legit shot.When you see the Royals having four Gold Glove finalists and three for the Silver Slugger, it only serves to underscore how dreadful the pitching—particularly the bullpen—was this season.In a blink and you missed it transaction, the Chicago White Sox signed Alec Marsh to a minor league deal. The Royals released Marsh at the end of last month as they were getting their 40-man roster tidied up. He last pitched for the Royals in 2024, having missed time with shoulder soreness that became a shoulder impingement that became labrum surgery.When the Royals optioned him off the roster, I thought there was a chance he could return on a minor league deal, like the one he signed with the White Sox. Good luck to Marsh going forward. It has to be incredibly frustrating to miss two full seasons due to injury. I hope he can find a way to get back on the field in 2027.If you have an itch to watch live baseball, you can scratch it with the Arizona Fall League "Fall Stars Game" tonight on MLB Network. The Royals will be well represented with outfielders Angeibel Gomez and Zion Rose and with left-hander Justin Lamkin suiting up to represent the American League. Gomez, as you know is the second-youngest player in AFL history, has played mostly right field for the Surprise Saguros and hit .306/.390/.444 over 10 games. Just an exciting talent. Rose has hit .327/.493/.519 with two homers, two triples, 14 walks and 12 steals in 13 games for Surprise.Lamkin is in Surprise to make up innings he missed after dealing with shoulder issues this year. According to the write-up at MLB.com:(Lamkin) has been exceptional at getting ahead of hitters early with his fastball while showing two good breakers in his curveball (a relatively new pitch) and slider, leading to a 3.52 ERA and a 0.78 WHIP in four starts (15 1/3 innings).The game is scheduled to start tonight at 7 CST.

item.title: The Blue Jays Have An Asshole, And His Name Is Anthony Santander
item.author: Chris Thompson
item.content:encoded: Outfielder Anthony Santander appears to be a brain-poisoned, red-pilled moron and an Islamophobe. On Wednesday, Santander shared to his Instagram account a video warning about America's impending adoption of Sharia law, and another about Muslims being inherently violent. The videos stayed up until Thursday, by which time they had drawn the attention of his employer, the Toronto Blue Jays. Santander then scrubbed the videos, and the Blue Jays issued a somewhat limp statement, assuring fans that "individual comments do not represent our organization's values and beliefs."Santander seems to be getting his news from bad sources. Laura Loomer, the deranged right-wing carnival barker, told her too-many Twitter followers Tuesday night that "America is over," and falsely claimed that the midterm blue wave swept into Congress people who "openly talk about their hatred of America, love of communism, and support for Sharia law." The videos shared by Santander originated with the Instagram accounts of The American Truth Project and Nuhu Simon Jatau. The former is a right-wing propaganda dispensary whose website is littered with headlines like "300 MILLION DEAD AMERICANS" and "SATANIC PRAYER." The latter is a very obviously psychotic Nigerian man (a Lakers fan, to boot) who posts swirly-eyed videos claiming, among other things, that Muslims are pagans who worship Satan.You don't have to be so fully submerged in Christian-right paranoia in order to encounter outright, targeted Islamophobia, and from newsmakers and publications that project a superficially convincing, far less YouTube-coded, veneer of authority. Maya Sulkin of the Free Press posted a video Wednesday (now deleted) falsely claiming that Abdul El-Sayed, Michigan's senator-elect, delivered his victory speech in Arabic. Sulkin's video linked El-Sayed together with Ilhan Omar, representative from Minnesota, and Aber Kawas, a newly elected state senator from New York, to make the explicit case that America is under attack from, uhh, democratically elected American Muslims. "I wonder if this sounds like America to you," ponders Sulkin, twitching and quivering with panic. It was not until late Friday afternoon that the Free Press got around to dumping a correction onto Twitter, acknowledging that El-Sayed's speech was delivered in English, with three Arabic phrases thrown in. "The Free Press regrets the error," claimed the Free Press, falsely.

item.title: The story the legacy media stopped telling
item.author: 1axbp2golm42b2zpvtu6cdwkwmq5j68eilcogz@bf56x.hubspotemail.net
item.content:encoded: I have worked on campaigns for more than 30 years. I’ve represented presidential candidates who won and who lost, as well as candidates in Senate, House and gubernatorial races, in their moments of greatest joy, deepest despair and greatest uncertainty.Elections are not won or lost in one night. They are the product of campaigns, cultural shifts, referendums on those in power and hopes for the future. But they are also the result of voting laws and rules.If there is one lesson from 2026, it is that the rules of voting matter as much as anything else.Donald Trump spent countless hours and taxpayer dollars trying to rig the rules to hold on to power. The Department of Justice systematically attacked our elections through lawsuits, intimidation and lies.In the end, they failed, because lawyers litigated, election workers did their jobs and the American people voted.Sadly, the legacy media largely ignored the real stakes of these long, hard-fought legal battles to protect voters and voting rights in the midterm elections.Their coverage focused on the horse race and on who stood to benefit from each challenge. It ignored the question of right and wrong: Trump was trying to undo democracy, while those of us fighting back were working to protect it.I am proud that Democracy Docket never shied away from these fights, and I am grateful that you were right there with us.I started Democracy Docket in 2020 because the legacy media was failing to cover the onslaught of GOP attacks on free and fair elections. Today, more than 500,000 readers turn to us for news about what’s happening in the courts.Throughout the midterm elections, from the gerrymandering battles to the post-election litigation, Democracy Docket’s team worked around the clock to bring you up-to-date news and analysis about efforts to subvert election results and disenfranchise voters.No one followed the Justice Department’s lawsuits attacking our voting system more closely, and no other outlet provided the same depth of analysis.In addition to my day job as a lawyer in these fights, I wrote essays and provided breaking news analysis on a near-daily basis through livestreams, during which I answered your questions.That’s because Democracy Docket has never been a one-way platform. Speaking with you and hearing your feedback has always been a priority.Our work is far from over. In many ways, the hardest part is still ahead. Ballots are still being tabulated, certification is ongoing and legal challenges remain.Democracy Docket is on the ground in Mississippi, and we are watching and reporting on close elections around the country.Though the work continues, we could not have gotten through this moment without you. Your messages inspire me, your optimism motivates me and your support keeps this work going.Our members keep Democracy Docket’s website and podcasts free for everyone. Free content is core to our mission, which makes our Premium members essential. They powered us through the midterms, and they will power us through what comes next.Premium members also receive my written analysis and invitations to members-only events. If you read my analysis while our paywall was down during the midterms, you already know what that includes.If you’re not able to become a Premium member right now, I understand. As always, thank you for being a subscriber and reader. But if you do upgrade, I would deeply appreciate it.Our work together is just beginning, and I’m honored to have you by my side during this new dawn for our democracy.

item.title: datasette #3046: Don't serve link: rel=next HTTP headers to Firefox for HTML pages
item.author: Simon Willison
item.content:encoded: I was looking at the Firefox network panel today when I noticed that requests to a Datasette table page were triggering an HTTP prefetch to the next page of rows in that table.This was happening because Datasette pages serve an HTTP header like this:link: <https://latest.datasette.io/fixtures/compound_three_primary_keys?_next=a%2Cd%2Cv>; rel="next"This is bad. A tiny fraction of the visitors to one of those pages will click the "next" link, which means for everyone else their browser is fetching unnecessary data and the Datasette server is having to render an entire page that then gets thrown away.I dug in and learned that Firefox has an issue that has been open for 24 years about this behavior...And one of the early comments on that issue links to my blog post from 2002 complaining about this feature. I hadn't just forgotten that I had written about it, I had forgotten the feature entirely!

item.content:encoded: After two or three days of stupor and disorientation Donald Trump has reverted to form, as predicted, and has reacted to his historic repudiation by leaning into the powers of the presidency to reassert power and dominance. So far, they are mostly assertions and visual, thin performances not so much of power but of aggression, which seem more risible because the power is so clearly draining out of him. Trump appointed Stephen Miller as his new White House chief of staff. Today he has offered the press secretary position to Dana White, CEO of UFC, the mixed martial arts promotion company, who Trump lauds as “the Great Dana White, a violent Fighter and Warrior.” Trump is asking him to take on the press secretary role with a series of MMA fighter “assistants,” one or more of whom is associated with a Chechnyan warlord. We say “offered” because Trump seems to have offered White the job and then asked him via Truth Social to accept the job.

item.title: Terry Pratchett's Study

item.content:encoded: But horizontal wealth means not letting your increased income dictate your tastes. You like books and now you have money? Buy more books! Change those catenary bookshelves for good hardwood ones! In my case, build a library extension to your office. And, of course, you buy what will be useful for that most wonderful of pursuits, blind research, which is research without direction for the sheer joy of it.(Original source is his book A Slip of the Keyboard - this linked blog post quotes that bit.)

item.title: Steve Hilton is convinced he's going to win. Hahahaha.
item.content:encoded: There’s a midterm election coming on Nov. 3, which includes a race here in California to determine who will replace Gov. Gavin Newsom. On the blue side of the ticket is unremarkable Democrat Xavier Becerra, whose chief positive attribute is that he is not a Republican. On the red side is Steve Hilton, an immigrant from the U.K. who gained U.S. citizenship in 2021. Hilton’s most high-profile political experience came back in the early 2010s, when he served as an adviser to then-U.K. prime minister and alleged porcine enthusiast David Cameron. But that experience, plus a lengthy stint as a commentator for Fox News, was enough to convince Hilton that he not only should run for governor, but that he WILL be the state’s next governor.On the surface, he makes for an attractive candidate. Hilton is good company, and when I met him, he was as good at explaining the issues, as you would expect a seasoned broadcaster to be. He’s even reaching out to the gay community, albeit in somewhat awkward fashion. Listen to the man talk and you might come away thinking he’s a Democrat.But Steve Hilton is not a Democrat. He’s a Republican, one who plans to give tax breaks to the wealthy, massively increase funding to the police and let artificial intelligence companies do basically whatever they want without fear of California regulation. Most importantly to me, he is backed by President and aspiring dictator Donald Trump. So, Hilton can’t run as a Republican, especially not in a state as firmly blue as California, without having to answer for that party’s standard-bearer. But God bless Hilton, he gave it a try, repeatedly, when I met with him in August. This was true right from my opening question, when I asked him why he wanted to run for governor here at all.Article continues below this ad“I love California and it’s obviously not working,” he told me. “Sixteen years of one-party rule, it’s a disaster. So we’ve got to turn things around.”“OK,” I shot back, “but why would I trust a Republican to change any of this, in this administration?”At this, Hilton feigned ignorance. “In which administration?”Article continues below this ad“The Trump 2 administration.”“I don’t see the relevance of that to California.”Hilton acknowledged none of those things. Instead, he continually portrayed himself as a heroic outsider. “I’m not the president,” he insisted, with a showman’s vigor. “I’m not him. I’m me.”Article continues below this adWhen I brought up the president later in our conversation, he complained to me, “I don’t know why you keep talking about Trump.”“That’s why I’m here,” I told him. “Because you’re a Republican. I want you to explain to me how you could possibly exist as a functional Republican with the standard-bearer of that party exercising a ridiculous amount of influence over the party and being a general, omniscient presence over the entire country, California included.”“Well, I think that description, it just doesn’t match the facts,” Hilton told me. The polls at the time implied that voters did not agree. When I met Hilton in August, he was trailing Becerra badly, so I asked him why he was running a campaign that was doomed to fail. “That gap [in the polls] is shrinking,” he said to me, with no lack of confidence. “The gap went from 25 to 18 in the Berkeley poll. What was the next one? Our own internal poll, down to 14 points. There’s a poll that we’re hearing about next week where the gap will be under 10%.” Article continues below this adHilton didn’t mention that he was quoting polls from before and after the primary, and the gap fell from 21 not 25, which is VERY much a Republican thing for him to do, but I still gave him the benefit of the doubt.“Let’s say the poll numbers hold and you don’t win the election,” I said to him. “Where would you go after this?”At this, he laughed. “I don’t know. I haven’t thought about it. I’m planning to win. I do believe that I’m going to be the next governor. I can see it. I believe it.”Article continues below this ad“Is that your ego talking? Have you convinced yourself?”“No, it’s California talking. It’s the conditions in our state.”“It’s not the polls talking.”“Yes, but we’re just at the start of the campaign. No one really pays attention until after Labor Day anyway. Everything points to this being a change election in California. That means that I will win the election. That is my strong expectation.”Article continues below this adBut that confidence only holds if Hilton pretends the Trump factor in this race isn’t significant. Surely the voters he’d met along the trail had told him as much. That’s why I asked him, “Have you not had voters talk to you specifically about what the president is doing?”That answer floored me. “Never?”Article continues below this ad“Literally never comes up,” Hilton boasted. “It’s ‘What are we going to do about the gas prices?’ Right now in California, you’ll see gas prices in the $5 to $6 range. If you go to Texas today, they’re in the $3 range. Same country, same president, same Iran war going on, vastly different gas prices. That’s entirely due to the policies that Democrats have pursued in California.”He’s partially correct, given that California’s gas prices are high partially because the state has the highest gas tax in the country, and its fuel standards increase costs for producers. But he again fails to acknowledge the role the Trump administration has played in driving up prices nationwide. It’s a form of denial that he’s shown many times over, from asking voters to ignore Trump’s endorsement of him after he accepted it, to attempting to soften his affection for other members of the MAGA herd, including the late Charlie Kirk. Hilton came to our meeting sporting a wristband honoring the fallen white supremacist. I asked him why he had it.“He was a good friend of mine, and someone gave it to me,” Hilton said about that. “So I just kept it.”Article continues below this ad“Did you like his way of going about things, because he was rather open about his views on race.”“I’m not sure what you’re referring to.”“Well, he was a friend of mine. I’m sure we all agree that we are friends with many people. That doesn’t mean we agree with 100% of everything they’ve ever said or done. You can still be friends with someone, just as I am with many Democrats. Don’t agree with them, but we’re friends.”Article continues below this adDo not count Becerra, the Democratic candidate, as one such friend. Hilton made sure to get in his jabs at Becerra in between all of my nagging questions. “We haven’t even talked about all the disqualifying factors for my opponent, who, in the words of [former Biden official] Susan Rice is ‘an idiot.’ You can’t have an idiot as governor of California.” I asked if he thought Becerra was especially idiotic given the current level of stupidity in the Trump administration, but he quickly sidestepped. “I don’t know. You’d have to ask Susan Rice. I don’t know why she called him an idiot.”Article continues below this ad“Well, you just said it was a great quote about him, so you must think he’s an idiot, too.”“I’m just telling you what people who have experience of working with him say. She also called him a ‘bitch-ass,’ whatever that means exactly.”“I think you know what a bitch-ass means.”“I actually, truly don’t know exactly what that means.”Article continues below this adHe must have learned in the interim. Because one week ago, Hilton faced off against Becerra in the only televised gubernatorial debate prior to the election. There, he brought up the “bitch-ass” comment from Rice directly to his opponent. He also constantly took umbrage anytime Becerra tried to link him to the president.“All you ever say is ‘Trump, Trump, Trump,’” he admonished Becerra. “That’s nothing but an insult to every Californian who is desperate for something to change in this state.”Article continues below this adIf voters here are desperate for a change, they’re not buying Hilton as the face of it. Two weeks after Labor Day, he is now down against Becerra by 25 points. I don’t think he’s going to win this election. Because when you’re a Republican, there’s no hiding it.

item.title: Could SCOTUS’ voting rights debacle hand Mississippi’s Dem a win?
item.author: 1axcjj8dy42g4omg9ymsnd2m6ms1wmqvc0yxur@bf56x.hubspotemail.net
item.content:encoded: It has been 156 years since Mississippi elected the first Black United States senator in American history. The state may soon see its second Black senator after voters flocked to the polls in defiance of the state’s restrictive voting system and a wider gerrymandering campaign across the South.Not three weeks after the Supreme Court erased significant portions of the Voting Rights Act, Mississippi’s Republican state leaders began gerrymandering.In churches, classrooms and courtrooms, there was a resurgence of a fight indicative of more than just a moment in time. Lydia Grizzell, the ACLU of Mississippi’s policy director, described the group’s work and ensuing impact in the months after Louisiana v. Callais as nothing short of historical.“I want America to think about this moment like the moment in which the Civil Rights movement was at its peak,” Grizzell told Democracy Docket.

item.title: This Week In Stupid: November 7 edition
item.author: Jeff Tiedrich
item.source: everyone is entitled to my own opinion
item.content:encoded: As another stupid week comes to a close here in America, let’s look back at the dumbest fucking shit that happened.Monday: big strong senators with tears in their eyes“I went to Best Buy this afternoon. I walked in, and three people there were almost in tears, expressing shock, ‘what has happened to our state?”All righty. Let’s do a quick fact check, because we really need to know: Did this happen? Did big, strong Texans, their cowboy hats slung low over their foreheads in order to hide their tear-stained eyes like few thought possible, actually come up to Ted Cruz and go, ‘Sir! Sir! Please tell us — what has happened to our state? Sir!’Of course this didn’t fucking happen, and the fact that the whole world is laughing at Ted Cruz and his stupid little story right now is why the entire MAGA movement is going to melt away the moment that Dear Leader goes gently into that good night.Whose bloated cankles are going to step into Donny’s clown shoes, after he’s gone? Who’s going to say literally the most idiotic shit imaginable, but in a way that makes the cultists swoon? That’s Donny’s one super-power, and no one one else in the MAGAverse has it.Do you imagine the Esteemed Senator Fidel Cancun is going to pull that off? Oh please, bro has negative charisma. His own daughter cringes.Tuesday: big strong conspiracy theorists with tears in their eyesTuesday was Election Day, and the cultists are still trying to figure it out. ‘How the fuck could this happen to us?’“I’m just going to say it right now. I have tried to salvage Trump. I’ve invested so much. Maybe I was blind to it. I think he’s the ultimate Democrat sleeper cell, and he works for them. And he was a Democrat before. I’m going to say it right now. He’s not that r*****d. He did this on on purpose. That’s what I believe.”Sure, why not. It all makes perfect sense to me. The Democrats secretly run a brain-dead stumblefuck for president , so that he can break the entire country — enriching himself in the process — after which Chuck Schumer and Hakeem Jeffries will just waltz in and sweep up whatever’s left over. I can’t believe no one’s ever connected those dots before.Oh, Alex, you sad little mope. Cope harder, my man. Cope harder.Wednesday: big strong found objects with tears in their eyes“There were a lot of people who voted for a dictator. He wanted to be a dictator on Day One, a lot of people said ‘good.’ You know, lock up crooked, deport the whole country. But that didn’t happen. That’s why the base didn’t show up in South Carolina and Mississippi.”Hey, wait a minute. How did that clip get in there? Because check it out — What’s going on here? Is Jesse auditioning for a slot on MS-NOW? Or is he so depressed that he forgot to do his ‘look at me, I say stupid shit on television’ court jester act?My whole world no longer makes sense to me.Thursday: big strong chucklefucks with tears in their eyesOkay, I’m going to call it right here and now: Abdul El-Sayed Derangement Syndrome is a thing. Just look at the dude. He’s young. Fit. Good looking. Smart. Charming. Funny. Articulate. You can’t win against all that shit. You can’t even compete against it, and it’s driving the MAGAsphere absolutely fucking insane.“El-Sayed comes off as a clown. Like one of these guys with an inferiority complex who needs to do this constant puffing all the time. It’s embarrassing.”Really, Dan? Tell us more. How does El-Sayed come off like a clown? Does he slather his sweaty, putrefying face with a half gallon of burnt cork, and then top it with some cotton-candy rat’s nest of a fright wig?How does El-Sayed puff himself up? Does he dance as if he were jacking off two invisible giraffes?Pure projection. At the end of the day, it’s all these shitweasels have left.Oh, and speaking of an inferior clown who needs to puff himself up, Dan — Folks, November is Abdul El-Sayed Derangement Syndrome Awareness Month. Won’t you please help find a cure, so that fuckwads like Danny Bingobongo don’t ever again have to karate-chop the air?Friday: the further adventures of Some Fucking Idiot™On Friday, some fucking idiot announced that Susie Wiles had been sent to a big farm upstate where she’ll have lots of room to run around, and that undead White House advisor Nosferatu McGoebbels had been promoted to Chief of Staff, because That’ll teach you not to laugh at the fucking idiot, and call him a loser. The fucking idiot had one public appearance on his official schedule for Friday: a speech at the Kennedy Space Center in Cape Canaveral, Florida.Before the thing started, was the fucking idiot presented with some fake gold-plated award that was invented just for the occasion? .Did the fucking idiot simply shit out his standard campaign speech, even though the election is over? .Did the fucking idiot repeat his latest whiny, needy talking point? .Did the fucking idiot mangle common words that any average four-grader could have aced? .Overall, was the the fucking idiot a sweaty, incoherent mess who told long, pointless stories with no clear beginning, middle or end? ?By the way, after the speech, the press did actually try to get an answer from the fucking idiot about why his administration was apparently going , sending threatening letters to conservative groups about monitoring their media appearances. The fucking idiot pretended to know nothing about it.But even though the fucking idiot was right there in front of them, not one reporter stood up to ask, ‘what the fuck is wrong with you?’How fucking idiotic is that?And now, let’s put a close to This Week in Stupid and reward ourselves with some Daily Claudia.Here’s Baby Kate and her mom, in the back yard of our old house in Hastings, early 1990s.This last one’s from some ocean-side New England inn, on October 19, 2003. There’s Katie, in the mirror.Have a non-stupid Saturday, everyone.here’s your daily reminder that I can be found on Blue Sky at this link.this is going to be my closing message for the foreseeable future:practice self-care. do what you need to do to keep sane. if that means you need to disengage with my daily posts for a while, I get it. this community of ours will still be here when you return.to all the people who have signed on in the days since the election, . settle in as we all try to deal with the shitfuckery that’s ahead of us.we are all in this together, and we are all here for each other.

item.title: Where’s Cindy? The Curious Part-Time Campaign of Cindy Hyde-Smith
item.author: Josh Marshall
item.source: Josh Marshall – TPM – Talking Points Memo
item.content:encoded: It now seems pretty clear that Scott Colom (pronounced c’l-O-m or like ‘cologne’ but with a final m instead of an n) is going to be the next senator from the state of Mississippi — not called yet but getting close. He would be the first Democrat elected from Mississippi since 1982 and the first Black senator since Blanche K. Bruce who served from 1875 to 1881. But one striking thing about the claims of victory from Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith, which manage to be both aggressive and half-hearted, is that as far as I can tell she has yet to appear in public since Election Day. I’m not even sure she’s done any media call-ins. Her first Twitter comment was written in the third person, as though the staffer who wrote it couldn’t even bother to pretend it was Hyde-Smith writing it. This turns out to be a through-line continuing from the campaign itself.We’re already wise to the way the building Blue Wave in 2026 exposed a number of Republican incumbents who simply weren’t ready for prime time as candidates but had gotten by pretty much unchallenged on Republican dominance of their states. Outgoing Senator Roger Marshall is the poster-boy for this dynamic. But Marshall at least mobilized late and mounted a campaign — a really comically bad campaign but still a campaign. Reviewing the wreckage of Hyde-Smith’s apparent defeat, it really seems like she was at best a part-time candidate and that really over-states her involvement in the election.

item.title: A Black veteran was beaten blind. Orson Welles vowed to solved the case.
item.author: bounce-mc.us1_388705.10708897-d186966748@mail155.sea81.mcsv.net
item.content:encoded: In 1946, a Black Army veteran was returning from World War II when a white police officer pulled him off a Greyhound bus and beat him blind. The details were fuzzy. No one was sure about the identity of the police officer. The veteran, Isaac Woodard, didn’t even know what town he was in when it happened. Radio host Orson Welles learned about the shocking crime and pledged to find the officer who did it. “We’ll call the policeman ‘Officer X,’” Welles said on his Sunday evening program. “He might be listening to this; I hope so. Officer X, I’m talking to you. Wash your hands. Scrub and scour, you won’t blot out the blood of a blinded war veteran.”, the podcast brings us Woodard’s story, from his beating to the outrage that prompted the military’s desegregation. And to understand the experience of a Black servicemember today, we speak with Kyle Bibby, a Marine Corps veteran and co-founder of the Black Veterans Project.

item.title: How Earth Lost a Billion Years of Its History
item.author: Becky Ferreira
item.content:encoded: Welcome back to the Abstract! Here are the studies this week that drew a blank, felt the squeeze, played the queen, and made donkey-bull love.First, scientists shed new light on how Earth ended up losing more than a billion years of its geological record, a puzzle that has resisted explanation for decades. Then: octopuses in tight spots, a topless spear-brandishing Celt, and a tale of unlikely tail.“Blank Space” (Earth’s Version)Earth doesn’t trouble itself too much with keeping intact archives. With its tectonic activity and erosive forces, our planet is constantly wiping out huge chunks of its own memory, creating gaps in the geological record called unconformities. The Great Unconformity, the largest gap of this kind, reveals that Earth straight-up deleted more than a billion years of strata, for reasons that remain hotly debated and mysterious. Sandstone that dates back to the Cambrian period some 538 million years is often found directly on top of ancient “basement” rocks that date back anywhere from 1.2 billion to 1.8 billion years ago. This missing layer shows up around the world, hinting that it was erased by a global event. Now, scientists have placed the origins of the Great Unconformity deep inside Earth’s mantle, during the tectonic tumult of supercontinent breakup.“The cause or causes of the Great Unconformity are unknown,” said authors Santosh Dhungana and Nicolas Flament of the University of Wollongong. “The proposed mechanisms include extensive glacial erosion during Snowball Earth (about 720–635 million years ago), rifting and plume activity, sea-level fall and mantle-driven dynamic topography.” “These processes have not been dynamically tested, with limited comparison between global models and global datasets to explain the spatial distribution of the Great Unconformity,” the team added. To fill the knowledge gap about the geological gap, the researchers ran models of the formation and breakup of ancient supercontinents during the eons preceding the Cambrian period, when complex life rapidly proliferated in Earth’s seas. Massive landmasses were pushed upward by motions in Earth’s mantle during this time. Exposed to erosive forces such as weather, glaciers, and eventually oceans, they became sanded down over time, creating the vast void. “Our models explain why the Great Unconformity is best preserved in North America and show that it is a first-order surface expression of deep geodynamic processes that transformed global landscapes and sediment fluxes,” the team concluded.Scientists will no doubt continue to of this planet-wide memory lapse, but there is consensus that the same mechanisms also set the stage for the emergence of complex life during the Cambrian. No matter what caused the Great Unconformity, we partly owe our existence to it today. Putting the squeeze on octopuses We’ll move now from massive gaps in Earth’s memory to tiny gaps that octopuses can somehow squeeze through. These tentacled escape artists can famously maneuver their way through passages that seem impossibly small relative to their bodies, an ability that has spawned a subgenre of viral videos.Now, scientists have discovered the secrets of “octopus-squeezing behavior” by observing two species—the common octopus () and the Mayan octopus ()—navigating small holes in laboratory containers. “Our study demonstrates that octopuses employ two primary strategies, 3-step and 4-step, for squeezing through narrow spaces,” said researchers led by Wenci Xin of the National University of Singapore. “The key distinction between these strategies lies in whether the body is squeezed separately from the arms.” The first two steps were probing the aperture and then shifting a few arms through it. Navigating the tightest spaces required breaking up the final passage into two parts: Pulling the remaining arms to the other side, and then compressing the mantle behind the head so they could fit through last.In addition to documenting these amazing feats of flexibility in nature, the study is the perfect excuse to revisit the classic episode “Squeeze.”When Rome invaded Britain 2,000 years ago, they had the help of an inside man—or was it an inside ? In a new article, an archaeologist makes the case that the British king Verica, who aided the Roman invasion of their own homeland, was actually a queen that has been misgendered lo these many centuries. Miles Russell of Bournemouth University argues that Verica was a woman based in part on the leader’s Latin name, which ends in the suffix “a” which is common for women, as opposed to names ending in “-us” for men. Coins also depict Verica using “slender, bare-breasted equestrian figures that appear irrefutably female in contrast to the overtly masculine warriors on the issues of Iron Age rulers like Tasciovanus and Caratacus,” according to Russell. Women leaders weren’t unheard of in Celtic Britain, as evidenced by the queens Cartimandua and Boudica, who lived in the same century as Verica. Regardless of whether Verica was among their ranks, this leader was a consequential figure in the Roman takeover of Britain. Achille and Patroclo: More than friends Scientists who were conducting fieldwork on monkeys in Ethiopia serendipitously stumbled upon a very different discovery—a tender same-sex relationship between a bull and a donkey.Achille, a bull, and Patroclo, a donkey, belong to different owners, but they graze together by day. Despite the availability of other males and females in their pasture, this pair has developed a strong socio-sexual bond that includes nuzzling, licking, and Achille sexually mounting Patroclo.“Patroclo frequently presented his hindquarters toward Achille and nipped him,” said researchers led by André Beirão da Cruz of the University of Pisa. “In the only two instances in which Achille approached and mounted another male donkey, this individual showed clear avoidance behaviours and displayed threatening facial expressions (e.g. ear flattening), which were never observed in Patroclo during the 51 mountings (34 with intromission) with Achille.”Same-sex sexual behavior is extremely common in nature and has a wide variety of possible explanations, including social cohesion, mistaken identity, or lack of access to opposite-sex mates. But what Achille and Patroclo have is special. Despite being different species and having alternate mating options, the pair share a highly selective and reciprocal social and sexual bond. “Although interpreting this behaviour is challenging, the mounting attempts, taken together with the repeated and mutual affiliative interactions between the two animals, may signal the quality of their relationship” and “the strength of the animals’ social bond,” the team concluded.In addition to this heartwarming tale, the study goes to show that you never know what you might find when you chase your goals. The researchers were there to watch geladas, but it turned out those primates weren’t the only animals monkeying around.Thanks for reading! See you next week.

item.content:encoded: Creativity doesn’t drive my blogging; software does. So daily.baty.net is back in rotation and is once again built using Tinderbox.Tinderbox is special. I've been preaching this for more than 20 years. However, my use of Tinderbox has slowed down in recent years due to the distraction that is Linux. I felt I needed to move away from macOS-only software. I shouldn't have.I've been "going ham" with Tinderbox recently, and it feels good. I used to in its Map views, but that was back when I was working. Now, I use it mostly as a fancy outliner (it's a really good outliner) and as a blogging tool.Tinderbox manages daily.baty.net. For a minute I was using Eleventy, but no longer. Tinderbox's export features are complex, and sometimes I get lost, but they're also very flexible and powerful.Long story short, when I'm experiencing the rush that comes with rediscovering Tinderbox, I want to use it for everything, so I brought it back and I'm posting daily notes there instead of journal entries here.In case you were wondering.

item.title: Pete Hegseth’s holy war on “weirdos” targets most Americans
item.content:encoded: Pete Hegseth is odd. This isn’t just a personal opinion, though there’s no doubt that he gets widely mocked for his carefully cultivated public persona, which is a mix of megachurch preacher, gym rat and Robert Duvall’s napalm-huffing character in “Apocalypse Now.” The fact that the defense secretary is different is simply a statistical reality.It’s not just that he’s a white evangelical Christian, a group that, according to PRRI, makes up only 13% of the population. Hegseth’s church, the Communion of Reformed Evangelical Churches, is extreme even for the right, with a leader who argues against women’s suffrage and teaches that slavery was the height of “mutual intimacy and harmony” between the races. Even within MAGA, those remain fringe positions, despite great efforts by some Christian nationalists to reignite “debate” on such long-resolved issues. All this means it’s hard not to laugh when Hegseth pontificates about his hatred of “weirdos.” Although he has a war to fight in Iran, somehow he finds time to focus his attention on what he clearly sees as the greater battle: remaking the military according to the demands of his very white, very male, very right-wing vision.““Wimps,” “radicals” and “weirdos” are more ambiguous pejoratives, but Hegseth’s recent actions suggest his definitions are expansive enough to cover the vast majority of Americans. He’s been on a firing spree, demanding a 20% cut of the Pentagon’s top brass in an apparent effort to expunge those he deems “woke.” The move comes after nearly two years of blocking promotions for and pushing out Black and female military leaders. Hegseth also rewrote the list of religions recognized by the Pentagon, narrowing from over 200 faith categorizations to a mere 31 — 22 of which are Christian. He claims this is to simplify the bureaucracy, but his motives are likely more disturbing: to stigmatize non-Christians and restrict the definition of “Christian.” The Air Force is already forcing service members to register their religious beliefs under the truncated list, drawing criticism from atheists and others whose belief systems are not included as options. Last week, Hegseth upped the ante by announcing the formation of the Office of Religious Affairs “to strengthen the moral, ethical and spiritual readiness of our warfighters.” Despite boilerplate claims that this action will not “compel religious participation” or “diminish the free exercise rights” of service members, both the policies and pomp surrounding the announcement made it clear that the goal is to promote Hegseth’s version of Christianity — and shame anyone who does not adhere to it. The office will be run by the defense secretary himself and, in ominous language, promises to fund “research, technology, and analytical tools to support and assess spiritual fitness,” which sounds like a data-gathering operation to ensure troops meet Hegseth’s esoteric views on proper religious practice. “Taken together, this purge helps clarify what Hegseth means when he’s talking about “weirdos” and “wimps,” as well as other slurs like “t******s.” He’s hostile to women, the LGBTQ+ community, people of color and anyone who doesn’t adhere to his vision of conservative Christianity — although it’s worth noting that with his message of peace and love, Jesus Christ himself would not be accepted by Hegseth as a Christian.The secretary may have gone to Princeton University, but he hasn’t yet grasped the concept of irony. The people he deems “weirdos” far outnumber those in his narrow category, presumably of non-weirdos, many times over. Hegseth has tried to justify his position and rhetoric by arguing that a proper military should only contain “the real 1%” of supposedly superior people. But as Eliot Cohen of The Atlantic notes, this claim is ignorant of history. You need large numbers to win wars, which inherently means that armies can’t be elitist institutions.Hegseth has a real math problem on his hands. His “real 1%” of alleged non-weirdos is just not enough people to staff a modern military, especially in times of war. His solution appears to be to hit the road, trying to recruit more mini-Hegseths to enlist. On Sept. 19 he embarked on the Send Me Tour in an effort to reach out to people in white evangelical-heavy parts of the country with a Bible-heavy pitch about how Jesus wants them to fight for their country. Both the tour’s name and the secretary’s stump speech rely heavily on In a response video, Sen. Raphael Warnock, the Democrat from Georgia who is also an ordained minister with multiple theology degrees, didn’t mince his words. “Pete Hegseth is busy twisting the scriptures yet again . . . Those objectives, of course, are not remotely Hegseth’s. His creation of a hierarchy that places white, straight men at the top and relegates everyone else into an underclass of “weirdos” and “wimps” ignores the Bible’s historical context — and actual meaning. Anyone who doubts that can simply examine his behavior in office and his monomaniacal focus on sorting America’s service members into a worthy-unworthy dichotomy, based solely on how much they adhere to his own self-serving ideals of what a soldier should look like.

item.title: What voters have to say in nail-biting Mississippi Senate race
item.author: 1axcgslm4f3er3g2tx9ibv8eadk7727ynkpw33@bf56x.hubspotemail.net
item.content:encoded: After Democratic candidate Scott Colom met with supporters at a senior center, Democracy Docket spoke with Peggy Smith, 78, about the election’s significance to her.She recalled protesting for school integration in 1963. Now, she says she’s “ecstatic” how far Mississippi has come.“This is going to be a history-making decision if we come out — not if, but when — Scott comes out [on top],” she told Democracy Docket. “And it just reminds me of the years that we marched and that we fought for our state to come out on top.”Colom said he felt “confident” and urged voters to check if their ballots remain uncounted.“At some point we’ve got to accept reality. We’ve got to accept the will of the voters, we’ve got to follow the process, we’ve got to be patient, but at some point we just have to start the transition because the people of Mississippi — they’re going to need their junior senator to be ready to go on day one,” he said.

item.title: Double Down Miller
item.author: Josh Marshall
item.source: Josh Marshall – TPM – Talking Points Memo
item.content:encoded: President Trump’s decision to replace Chief of Staff Susie Wiles (a rare beacon of competence if not good values) with Stephen Miller confirms the predictable Trump storyline. Always double down. For maybe 48 hours Trump seemed stunned and drifting. Now he’s coming to from the smelling salts of ambient chatter about his political legacy concluding in disgrace and failure. We can’t know the future. But this is why Democrats can have realistic hopes of a second strong election in a row in 2028. Trump is making the characteristic decision of force feeding the country what it just spit up. We know this about Trump: he reacts to being dominated, owned and mocked by casting around for ways to assert power and dominance. It’s as predictable with him as night follows day.

item.title: Caleb Williams Is Carrying All Of Chicago Sports On His Back
item.author: Ray Ratto
item.content:encoded: Caleb Williams is carrying an unimaginable burden, and it's not just the matter of being the last living quarterback in the NFL, or easing into his place as the best Chicago Bears quarterback in three quarters of a century while running the most prolific Bears offense in 50 years. It's been only eight weeks since his season began, and already he is the preeminent face of Chicago sports. This looks like high praise, but while that praise would be deserved where Williams is concerned, consider the context.Williams is not working against a deep field—not in the NFC North, which is the toughest division in the league, but in the town in which he works. There, his opposition is Northwestern's football team, which is 6-2 but unranked and unlikely to break through the upper crust of the Big Ten. The Cubs were routed from the postseason in the shortest possible amount of time, and the White Sox are still striking out despite their season having ended four weeks ago. The Sky are notable only for having turned Angel Reese into a useful player by trading her to another team. And the Bulls and Blackhawks are demonstrably god-awful, well within the margin for error for having a spectacular margin for errors. You know, like the post-election Republican mood.How god-awful, you ask, since you've been averting your eyes? The Bulls are 1-7, and are losing their games by an average of 18 points per game, which ranks as the largest margin of stinkage in NBA history, albeit in this admittedly minuscule sample; they are allowing the second-highest number of points per game ever. They will doubtless revert to a gentler if still depressing mean, as all non-expansion teams tend to do, but with a starting lineup of Caleb Wilson, Norman Powell, Josh Giddey, Matas Buzelis, and Jalen Smith, it would be foolish to rule out the 11-71 outcome for their season.
