item.title: Trump’s Alaska meltdown says it all
item.author: 1axbpx0vlef675kwd5p26396aqqssvrq070qub@bf56x.hubspotemail.net
item.content:encoded: Judging by his social media post, Donald Trump agrees with me, which is why he is focused on Alaska as his last chance to keep the Democratic Senate sweep — and his humiliating defeat — from growing any larger.Peltola holds a narrow lead, with more ballots still to be counted. What Trump continues to ignore is that those ballots will be counted and the results certified pursuant to state law. There is no legal path to reassigning votes.In the run-up to the election, Trump directed his Department of Justice to accomplish in court what he is still demanding on social media today. DOJ lost — badly. It filed an appeal to the Ninth Circuit but has taken no steps to seek immediate review or relief.The lawyers at DOJ no doubt understand what Trump does not: His effort to rig the Alaska Senate election failed. His assault on free and fair elections is over.Indeed, Trump and his cronies are now likely to face a Congress eager to conduct oversight of their abuses of power, and that oversight is certain to include their attacks on democracy.Nowhere will the administration face greater scrutiny than in the Democratic-controlled House of Representatives. While the Senate margins have garnered much of the attention, House Democrats romped from coast to coast.Before the election, Democrats were expected to take control of the House, but with somewhere between 225 and 235 seats. Democrats have already been declared the winners in more than 250 races, and that number continues to climb.No party has won more than 257 House seats in over three decades, a total Democrats reached in 2008. That came in a presidential election year, a historic one at that; meeting or exceeding that number in a midterm would be astounding.All of these victories are even more impressive given the obstacles Donald Trump put in the way of voters, election officials and Democratic candidates.He pressured big law firms to provide him with free legal services and intimidated them out of protecting voting rights. His Department of Justice launched more than 30 cases to undermine free and fair elections. He weaponized the criminal justice system against his political opponents.Yet despite all of that, Trump and his party not only lost but were thoroughly repudiated.There will be many theories about why Trump failed. Some will say it was the economy and affordability. Others will point to foreign wars or health care.Yes, those issues — plus corruption and democracy — helped motivate voters and shaped their choice of candidates. But none of it would have mattered if the machinery of elections had failed.As we celebrate the landslide repudiation of the GOP, we must remember how close we came to losing voters’ ability to elect the candidates of their choice.In the days ahead, I believe we will celebrate Democrats gaining Senate seats in Mississippi and Alaska. I expect House Democrats to surpass 257 seats.Once those results are certified and the celebrations have ended, it will be time for us to get to work. Never again should we have to fight the federal government to protect our elections. Never again should a president be empowered by his party to destroy democracy.This is the defining fight of our generation. As soon as my legal work in the remaining elections is done, I am ready to take it on right here at Democracy Docket. I hope you will join me.

item.title: Oldest Evidence of Getting High on Cannabis Discovered In 2,800-Year-Old Tomb: ‘Absolutely Crazy’
item.author: Becky Ferreira
item.content:encoded: Archaeologists have discovered the oldest direct evidence of psychoactive cannabis use in a Siberian tomb that dates back 2,800 years and was the site of human and horse sacrifices, according to a study published on Thursday in . During excavations of the tomb, a team found more than 1,400 cannabis seeds scattered around the remains of several Iron Age individuals, and even identified cannabinoids—including the active compound tetrahydrocannabinol (THC)—in a person’s preserved hair. Though humans cultivated cannabis for many millennia before the Iron Age, this is by far the earliest clear-cut proof that the plant was consumed for its psychoactive effects, which have made it one of the most widely used drugs in the world today.The discovery is “absolutely crazy,” said Gino Caspari, an archaeologist at the Max Planck Institute of Geoanthropology and the University of Bern who led the study, in a call with 404 Media. “People have been speculating a lot about psychoactive use of cannabis in the past, but to actually pin it down and prove it with soft tissue evidence of the humans involved—that is something very special.“That is an absolutely unique and extremely rare combination of evidence,” he added. Cannabis has a multifaceted history as a recreational drug and a pop cultural touchstone, as well as a traditional medicine that has been used for millennia by many cultures, including in China, Russia, and around the Mediterranean Basin. Humans began cultivating the plant as early as 10,000 years ago for its oil and fiber, but the origins of its specific consumption as a psychoactive substance is unclear. Cannabis was important to the Scythian culture, a horse-riding people that emerged on the Eurasian steppes in the 9th century BCE and became a major force in the subsequent centuries. The historian Herodotus described Scythian rituals that involved ceremonial burning of cannabis in enclosed spaces, and their cannabis residues and products have been found at Scythian archaeological sites.“Herodotus speaks about the Scythians being quite fond of cannabis in the first place, so this has always been in the back of our minds,” Caspari said. “But it is so incredibly rare to find well-preserved plant remains that this is not really something you can hope for or look for. This is ultimately complete luck and chance.”Now, Caspari and his colleagues have hit an archaeological jackpot at a tomb known as Tunnug 1, located in Siberia’s Uyuk River Valley. Six elite individuals are interred in the interior of the royal mound inside several tree-trunk coffins and wooden structures. They are mostly men, though one woman is also present. The mound is lined with remains of sacrificed humans, as well as dozens of sacrificed horses, close to the surface.As the team carefully worked through the layers of the burial, they found hundreds of cannabis seeds distributed around the bodies that were dated to the 8th century BCE. However, the real smoking blunt was the detection of cannabinols in preserved hair samples, including traces of THC, the most important mind-altering compound in cannabis. The results confirm contemporaneous accounts of Scythians as cannabis consumers who used the plant for purification and mortuary rituals. It’s possible that the people selected as human sacrifice consumed the drug to prepare them for their unenviable fate.“It being in a burial context, of course, there's a ritual aspect to it,” Caspari explained. “It might be a little bit more sinister, but this is speculation. We do have a lot of horse sacrifices and also some human sacrifices on the surface of the mound. And if you imagine humans being sacrificed, they usually don't like that very much. It might be advantageous to have them dosed a little bit, at least, to make the procedure a bit more humane, if you will.” “Of course, that is speculation,” he cautioned. “We don't have any written sources about that particular area, but that's at least one way we could go with our interpretation.”The researchers hope to learn more about the context and meaning of the cannabis use at Tunnug 1 through continued excavations and an analysis of more hair samples. What’s more, the team plans to conduct DNA analysis on the seeds, an approach that could yield new insights about the murky history of cannabis domestication and its early use as a psychoactive substance. This line of research could also shed light on modern cannabis strains, and may even be revived for new medicinal or recreational purposes. “We've already sequenced part of the seeds to unravel and disentangle the domestication history,” Caspari said. “Funnily enough, we don't even know what wild cannabis actually looks like because there has been so much intermixing and interbreeding since the 70s, when people started experimenting and trying to get more potent drug variants. Some of the initial landraces and the actual wild cannabis has been lost.”“Now, having DNA that's almost 3,000 years old, we will be able to take that step back into the past and see what an unaltered cannabis would have looked like,” he said. “In the ideal case, we might even be able to work together with the medical industry and bring some of these very ancient genetics back into cannabis production to potentially help people with very interesting and distinctive cannabinoid combinations.” Put that in your pipe and smoke it. Regardless of where future research into this ancient plant leads, this long-sought evidence of cannabis use thousands of years ago confirms the rich cultural legacy of the plant across time and space.“As an archeologist, I might be a bit biased here, but I think the history and cultural practices really do matter,” Caspari concluded. “I think our findings do indeed inform current discussions on legalization, on usage of medical cannabis—which is very much an ongoing discourse—and I think what we've been able to do with this study is provide an anchor, and show that there is this deep cultural history to the use of cannabis as a psychoactive drug.”

item.title: JD’s Warmed Over TuckerCarlsonism
item.author: Josh Marshall
item.source: Josh Marshall – TPM – Talking Points Memo
item.content:encoded: We’re seeing Republicans wrestle their way toward a first reaction to Tuesday’s genuinely historic electoral collapse. We saw it most clearly, with a heavily “nationalist” tinge, in JD Vance’s Tuesday sleight of hand about Trump’s Iran War. Vance’s argument is that Trump Two was basically going great, both substantively and politically, until Trump launched his war on Iran back in February. So the problem isn’t Trumpism but not to Trumpism with enough resolve. They only went wrong with the Iran War and even more Israel.Let’s start by noting that Vance’s gambit is just warmed over TuckerCarlsonism, or TuckCarlsonism without all the charisma. That is, racial/religious nationalism which has a specific beef with both Jews and Israel as part of a broader argument that America is a white and Christian country where non-whites and non-Christians are at best guests. You see this in Vance’s frequent references to “heritage Americans” and attacks on “ungrateful” Blacks and non-white immigrants who should be kicked out of the country if they don’t express gratitude clearly enough. This is a reality that deserves a lot of attention from Jews who are rightly concerned about antisemitism of various sorts on the left. Vance is not only clearly an antisemite personally but he is signaling that he plans to use that animus as a central lever of his drive to power.

item.title: Broadcast This Wemby Performance Into Space
item.author: Giri Nathan
item.content:encoded: In 1974, scientists sent into space a radio message encoding some basic facts about Earth and humanity. In the "Arecibo message," we shared with the cosmos some information about the shape and size of human beings, and the composition of human DNA. This year, we should run it back, but with the following video message instead. Any life form out there should know that they are welcome here after receiving this: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TGQUu-4g8pk Victor Wembanyama logged 52 points, 24 rebounds, and eight blocks in the San Antonio Spurs' thrilling 112-111 win over the Dallas Mavericks on Wednesday. It was a totalizing, two-way performance. Almost every possession offered a jump scare, as Wembanyama moved through space in ways heretofore unseen, or fused size and skill in ways not thought possible. Shots that would never been at risk of being blocked, at any previous point in NBA history, were in fact blocked. The 7-foot-4 guy blocking them was also beating his defender from the perimeter with a hesitation dribble. No one else mattered.

item.title: Has The Political Press Still Learned Nothing After a Decade of Trump?
item.author: David Kurtz
item.content:encoded: It’s been a jangly 36 hours watching America rise up against a wannabe authoritarian while the political press resorts to the same old tired tropes as if it were hungry to go back to the pre-Trump days or pretend they never happened.The U.S. press does a fine job covering democratic uprisings in foreign countries, but struggles mightily to cover them here at home.While the midterm elections here fit neatly into a pattern of right-wing defeats in the past few weeks in Serbia and Brazil, the mainstream media here — even after a decade — is still grasping to employ suitable language for the current authoritarian moment in the United States.The failures of the post-election news coverage mostly revolve around the embrace of worn-out horse-race campaign coverage and quickie post-election analysis in which losers lose because they’re idiots, and winners win because they’re geniuses.The inability to grapple open and honestly with the Christian nationalist neo-fascism of the Trump II presidency continues to bedevil domestic political coverage. In one of its post-election analyses, the NYT allowed that it was “a decisive rebuke to President Trump and his aggressive, often chaotic second-term agenda.”“Aggressive and often chaotic” are doing an awful lot of work there, as if the second term was an emotionally dis-regulated child with poorly medicated ADHD.Contrast that with the NYT’s description of Viktor Orban’s election defeat in April, which it credited with “breaking the momentum of a global nationalist revival promoted by President Trump.” The Hungarian election, it reported, was a “showdown between friends and foes of liberal democracy.”The coverage of an anodyne tweet by Vice President JD Vance yesterday captured the hunger of the political press to return to the coverage of old. Vance repeated what President Trump had already said — and what he would reaffirm after being asked about Vance’s tweet: that the Iran War cost them the election.Yet that somehow that become evidence of a dramatic break between Vance and Trump — even though Vance conceded little, took blame for nothing, and whitewashed the entire rest of the “aggressive, often chaotic second-term agenda,” to borrow a phrase. Perhaps the Vance team self-servingly nudged reporters toward that interpretation, as the publication of a “tick-tock” of the tweet by Politico might suggest.Blaming the Iran War is poised to become this cycle’s overly simplistic post-election narrative device. It offends almost no one, absolves the rest of the Trump II depredations, and misses its own anti-democratic origins.We’re at risk of having the blue wave chalked up merely to the pocketbook impacts of the Iran War and the Trump tariffs without connecting either of them to the underlying authoritarianism involved.The Iran War and the Trump tariffs, many of which (though not all) were struck down by the Supreme Court, were unilateral and illegal acts by the executive branch.Trump sidelined Congress in violation of the constitutional order. These weren’t merely bad or poorly executed policies. The founders knew from experience that this is the folly you get from giving too much power to one man.The notion that Republicans were victimized by Trump’s political “missteps” and “miscalculations” necessarily supposes that his rogue anti-democratic presidency is somehow disconnected from the horrible outcomes it produces. It also unwittingly implies that if the outcomes had been good, the means would have been fine.It’s the Economy AND Corruption, StupidMore Fun With Midterms DataAn assortment of interesting data points:“Republicans have not won a House of Representatives ‌seat in ⁠a district that Trump carried by less than 11 percentage points two years ago. … Democrats have won four seats that Trump carried by more than 15 percentage points.”—“Of about 3,000 counties where at least half the expected vote for the House has been tallied, all but about 170 saw Republican candidates run behind President Trump’s 2024 margin against Kamala Harris. The median county shifted about 11 percentage points toward the Democrats.”—“Republicans are only on track to flip one House seat, in Maine, that they didn’t redraw last year.”—Quote of the Day: Texas Edition“Calling it a dummymander is generous. This was more like moron-mandering. We went for five seats, won none, killed an incumbent, and handed Democrats a reason to turn out. Was living with Henry Cuellar really that hard?”—an anonymous Texas GOP strategist whom Politico described as “frustrated”Chart of the Day: Texas EditionDemocrats swept every demographic and geographic subgroup, according to the Times Voter Trends, except these (with the margin for Republicans): Impact on the New CongressDespite the Supreme Court’s decision in and subsequent aggressive Republican mid-decade redistricting to eliminate Black majority-minority districts, the impact on the new Congress is more nuanced than I might have expected.A total of 8 seats are going from Black to non-Black members, but four of those were held by Black Republicans, three of whom ran for higher office.A total of 6 seats are going from non-Black to Black members.Two Black members targeted by the GOP mid-decade redistricting scheme appear likely to survive: Shomari Figures (D-AL) and Don Davis (D-NC).The blue wave unquestionably muted the effects of … and I can’t emphasize this enough … .Before anyone interprets these numbers as minimizing what’s happened to Black voter representation in the South, was always understood to have more dramatic effects on state and local representation than on Congress. One of its biggest knock-on effects is to deprive Black candidates of access to the lower rungs of the political ladder that they can use to reach Congress.It’s also important to remember that the Voting Rights Act was about empowering Black , not Black candidates — so diversity among electeds is only a rough proxy for Black political power.This all comes against the backdrop of Rep. Hakeem Jeffries (D-NY) being poised to become the first Black speaker of the House and the addition of Juliana Stratton (D-IL) giving the Senate a record number of six Black senators, with a seventh if Scott Colom (D) wins in Mississippi.Mike Johnson Won’t Return as GOP LeaderOutgoing House Speaker Mike Johnson (R-LA) won’t seek to return as the House GOP leader in the next Congress, leaving Majority Leader Steve Scalise (LA) and Judiciary Committee Chair Jim Jordan (OH) to duke it out.This WaPo headline is a false dichotomy often used to manufacture storylines in political coverage: “Democrats face a choice on Trump come January: Confrontation or compromise.”Confrontation v. compromise is as flat, reductive, and imprecise as most of the dreary analysis of the moderate v. progressive fault line within the Democratic Party. There is understandable hunger for the prototypical Democratic officeholder to be more robust, combative, and decisive; but this kind of thin analysis sets up an easy gotcha for subsequent coverage that doesn’t reflect the strength of Democrats’ new majorities on the Hill.The reality is Democrats do not face a stark choice between confrontation and compromise. The can do both or either or neither. They get to pick when and where to fight their battles. They get to decide which hills to die on. They are in the driver’s seat.Besieged District Courts Get ReliefGeorgetown law professor Steve Vladeck, on the critical relief that a Democratic Congress can provide federal district courts:[T]he district courts have been under siege—even as they have been instrumental in standing up for the rule of law by fighting a classic rear-guard action. Unlike Blanche, they haven’t been trying to win a “war,” but rather just trying to hold the line in the hope that reinforcements would eventually be on their way.Thanks to Tuesday’s election results, those reinforcements are coming—in the form of a House of Representatives and Senate that will be just as interested in checking the executive branch … Races to Watch: Schadenfreude EditionObviously all eyes remain on the Mississippi and Alaska Senate races, which still hang in the balance, but longtime TPM readers will want to keep an eye on two House races that remain too close to call:: Republican Rep. , 48%, is trailing Democrat Eileen Laubacher, 48.7%, with 93% of the votes counted. Boebert, first elected to Congress in 2020, has been the archetypical MAGA-era GOP House member: a transgressive, attention-seeking wild child with a messy personal life.: Rep. (R) is trailing by 280 votes against Democrat Victoria Broderick, with 99% of the votes counted. DesJarlais predates the Trump era, having arrived in the Tea Party wave of 2010. He has persisted, shall we say, despite his own personal messiness being exposed earlier in his congressional career.

item.title: In the UK, Face Sitting Porn Might Land You in Jail
item.author: Samantha Cole
item.content:encoded: “I adore breath play. I love being strangled, suffocated and drowned, and I love strangling and suffocating others. Waterboarding: that’s my favourite,” Melissa Todd, a UK-based writer and sex worker, told me. “Many women do: it really isn’t only horrid men forcing us to do these dreadful depraved acts. Interrupting oxygen supply produces the most intense sensation of euphoria. I enjoy it in my private life, and I offer it in sessions too.” Starting tomorrow, she and anyone else in the UK distributing or possessing this type of content, even if it’s just recorded in the privacy of their homes and not for sale on a porn site, could face up to five years in prison. The maximum penalty for possession is “two years’ imprisonment for pornography that depicts strangulation or suffocation, or penetrative sexual activity between certain relatives,” according to the law, and “three years’ imprisonment for pornography depicting sexual activity involving a person who is, or is pretending to be, under 16,” with five years as the maximum penalty for publication of all of the above. Updates to the go into force on November 6. The law criminalizes a list of sexual acts, including downloading or making choking and incest roleplay porn. According to the law, it will be a criminal offense in England and Wales to possess or publish porn that “explicitly and realistically” depicts strangulation or suffocation, penetrative sexual activity between people who “a reasonable person would think are related, or pretending to be related, in a certain way” and sexual activity between people where “a reasonable person would think at least one person is, or is pretending to be, under 16.” Sixteen is the age of consent in the UK. “You have to speak up for porn you don’t like, as well as the porn you do, because otherwise the government will keep censoring more and more depictions of acts they don’t fancy."“The offences only capture pornography that shows people which appear, to a reasonable person, to be real,” the law states — whatever that means.The rest of the law is similarly vague in defining what’s criminalized. The “guidance” on the law says: “We consider that strangulation generally means one person applying pressure to another person’s neck,” and “We consider that suffocation will generally mean depriving a person of air in a way that affects their ability to breathe. Unlike strangulation, this does not require pressure to the neck. It could, for example, involve covering someone’s mouth and nose or compressing their chest.” This could mean anything from relatively common acts like face sitting or pushing someone’s face into a mattress, to gagging and more extreme breathplay generally left to professionals. The law says it’ll be left to the courts to decide.“This isn’t just about my personal preferences,” Todd said. “You have to speak up for porn you don’t like, as well as the porn you do, because otherwise the government will keep censoring more and more depictions of acts they don’t fancy. Even if you think strangulation is disgusting, immoral, dangerous, that is no reason to ban it. In a liberal democracy people must be allowed to behave in ways you think ridiculous and disgusting, in the hope that they in turn will extend the same courtesy to you. I don’t understand why people go skiing, or camping, or abseiling, but I’m happy for them to crack on with it. Consenting adults must be allowed to do whatever they want with their own bodies. It is illiberal and dangerous for the government to interfere."The effect of the law’s vagueness — as it has been in the US when legislators, payment processors and platforms similarly inflict poorly-defined terms on sex workers — is censorship and has a chilling effect on otherwise consensual legal activity between adults. It’s already happening: Adult clip site iWantClips warned, according to content creators using its platform, that in light of the law it’s banning a list of genres and acts: “iWantClips is required to remove certain categories of content from the platform for Artists located in the UK,” the message said, followed by a list including every kind of “smother” imaginable (including ass, foot, and breast smothering), plastic fetishes, all face sitting and specifically, face sitting in jeans, “butt drops,” and trampling fantasies. This isn’t the first time iWantClips has complied in advance of a threat to free speech: In October 2021, following new, strict moderation and documentation regulations set by Mastercard, the platform told creators they’d need to review their archives of content and make sure it was in compliance or risk a permanent ban. UK based porn performer and producer Vex Ashley, who owns the independent studio , told me that when the Crime and Policing Bill went through Parliament earlier this year, she examined her back catalog and found that the work she considers her “magnum opus,” which explores the sexual archetype of the mother, could contain criminal content under this law. “I had to go back and gut the film from the inside out,” Ashley told me. “It exists now in a very different form than it did when before. And obviously the law not only makes it illegal for me to publish it, but it also technically makes it illegal for me to possess the original cut of my film now, which just seems completely wild, considering that it’s me who is in it, and it's me talking about my own experience of my own sexuality.” Ashley noted that attacks on sexual freedoms always come for non-normative sex first: “kink, fetish, queer and trans bodies, anything a compliance team can’t file under vanilla,” she said. This, she believes, is part of an ongoing swing toward conservatism, authoritarianism, and control."Even if you're somebody who doesn't care about porn, who doesn't care about sex, but you do care about this rollout of conservatism that's being force-fed to us, you can defend people's right to fuck and be fucked, and to explore that through media"“The underlying message here is that actually, it's people's faults for being too horny, and that you should just control yourself,” she said. “That if you see this rollback in our sexual freedoms and this criminalisation of our sexual imaginations as wrong, you are just dangerous and perverted. Which is, I think, a swing back to old conservative and fascist ways of thinking about sex and freedom and bodily autonomy.” The “save the children” narratives that brought us harmful laws like FOSTA/SESTA in the US and an ongoing age verification nightmare around the world are at play with the Crime and Policing Act. In the UK, the Online Safety Act has forced people to verify their ages to use even non-sexually explicit parts of the internet. Looking at Pornhub from a UK-based IP address today, for example, you’d think it was a platform for podcasters and influencers; only once you log in and verify your age with a government ID and/or facial scan does the actual porn become visible. Independent creators and people dependent on online sex work in the UK will be the hardest hit by this new law. Dominatrixes that they’re expecting to take a financial hit. And even people and platforms outside of the UK may need to block users based in the UK from accessing their content to remain compliant. Many performers focus on specific niches to cater to audiences that seek out fetish content. But a lot of what’s being banned is already either banned by platforms or difficult to monetize, due to the extra-legal morality restrictions imposed by payment processors. Todd told me that while she enjoys the kind of content that’s now banned in the UK in her private life, she doesn’t bother uploading it to platforms where she could monetize it, because their terms of use have restricted most of it already. Those trying to comply with the law and avoid the threat of jail time face a task. The law's guidance makes it clear that possession and publication apply retroactively. “It's easy to talk about pornography as though it's a constantly replenished stream of disposable content, but for many performers it represents years of work and a significant investment of time and money,” Todd said. “A back catalogue can be an important source of continuing income. If material has to be removed, that isn't simply a matter of changing what you film next week; it can mean losing an asset you've spent years creating.” “Sex is a vital part of the human experience and it deserves exploration through storytelling, through media, through creation, in the same way that any other part of our experiences is,” Ashley said. “And that is not going to always be super comfortable. Sex is this very complicated, very vulnerable, very powerful thing, and it brings up a lot of things for different people.” Deciding, as a society, that it’s not worth defending or thinking deeply about is doing us all a disservice, she said — and comes at the cost of sex workers’ safety and freedom. Faced with potential prison sentences for having a face sitting video stored on a hard drive, the freedom in this case is very literal. “Even if you're somebody who doesn't care about porn, who doesn't care about sex, but you do care about this rollout of conservatism that's being force-fed to us, you can defend people's right to fuck and be fucked, and to explore that through media... I think you can defend it even if you think it's complicated.”

item.title: Leadership Dispatch: Bad surprises are bad
item.author: bounces+p9ugg2oe7li9hdkx6n2aqhpp0kw46trhklpz@ckespa.joshdoody.com
item.content:encoded: This week's Leadership Dispatch is about avoiding bad surprises. Good leadership is often about : You have to decide when to share bad news and when to handle it yourself. But you should always strive to avoid sitting on bad news so long that it becomes a bad surprise for your team.If you see bad news coming, don’t sit on it and hope things change for the better. Make sure you communicate that bad news early so the team can either prevent it or plan for it.It can be very easy to think you might save the situation before it gets bad, or that maybe things won’t turn out as bad as you expect. Hope is not a strategy. The longer you wait, the worse the surprise.How much you share will depend on whether you’re sharing up, sharing with co-leaders, or sharing with the team you’re leading. When sharing up and with co-leaders, share more and share faster. When sharing with the team you’re leading, share more selectively, but do not allow your team to be blindsided by bad news.You should also strive to share bad news along with some sort of plan or at least a suggestion to prevent or mitigate it. It’s much easier to receive bad news if it’s paired with a plan of action.

item.title: All we want are Democrats who’ll fight the fascists. Is that too much to ask?
item.author: Jeff Tiedrich
item.source: everyone is entitled to my own opinion
item.content:encoded: ‘You’re not a wartime Consigliere.’That’s Michael Corleone’s famous line from The Godfather, in which he explains to Corleone family counselor Tom Hagen that shit’s about to get real, and you don’t have what it takes.Know who else isn’t a ? Hakeem Fucking Jeffries, the Man Who Would Be Speaker of the House. Jeffries couldn’t his way out of a paper bag. I’m not even sure he understands what the actual job entails.Morning Joe: “Donald Trump said ‘I am your retribution,’ and he got wiped out. How do you now say, ‘hey, let’s not look behind us. We’re going to focus on bringing costs down’?”Hakeem Jeffries: “The American people don’t want us to get even, they want us to get things done on their behalf.”Holy shit, that sounds like a carefully-rehearsed line, doesn’t it? Why? I’ve never understood this pathological compulsion of Democratic leadership to go out the morning after every election and immediately piss all over everyone’s corn flakes. Is it too much to ask, to let us savor a victory for one whole day, before you start shitting all over everything?Why this need to assure us that there won’t be any ? No one’s asking for ‘retribution.’ What we want is . We’ve just lived through two years of the greatest lawlessness and corruption from a federal government that this country has ever experienced — big strong corruption with tears in its eyes — and now it’s time for some accountability. That’s not Preznit Fuckwit spent two years treating the US Treasury as his personal cash machine, fattening his wallet at our expense. We the People are struggling to make ends meet, while Dear Leader is somehow now a billionaire. Calling him to account for that is not Holding Piss-Drunk Pete Kegstand accountable for clownfucking us into an unwinnable war that destroyed our military readiness and set the world’s economy teetering on the edge of a crash, that’s not Holding everyone at Homeland Security accountable for masked ICE thugs disappearing innocent people into Salvadoran slave labor gulags, or leaving them shot to death on the street, that’s not It’s getting fucking justice, and it’s high time we had a little around here.How did Hakeem Jeffries allow himself to get manipulated by that useless pantload Morning Joe into disavowing ?Could it be because he’s ?You know who else isn’t a ? Chuck Fucking Schumer. He’s been proving it every day through his impotent lack of action. Schumer’s a great guy to have around if there’s absolutely nothing at stake.Need someone to speak at the dedication of a new post office? Chuck’s your man. Need someone to make sure all the procedural i’s are dotted and t’s are crossed in some piece of shrimp boat legislation? Here comes Chuck!Do you need someone to fight fascism? Chuck’s your— wait, where the fuck did Chuck go? He was here a minute ago.He’s probably busy writing a strongly-worded letter.Fortunately, we do have Democrats who aren’t so tone deaf, and do know how to say — and do — the right things.In case you somehow missed it in yesterday’s post, let me just leave this right here.That’s Rep. Robert Garcia, the Democrat who is now the incoming chairman of the House Oversight Committee. He posted that Tuesday night, after winning his own reelection.Know who Rep. Garcia replaces as Oversight Chair? This rake-stepping fuckwit, Comer Fudd.Is that an upgrade, or what? Imagine going from clownish side-show hearings involving Hunter Biden’s freakishly-oversized trouser trout, to actual investigations into how companies that Donny’s felonious failsons are invested in ended up getting billions of dollars in government defense contracts. You want to talk about an actual crime family? Boy, have I ever got one for you.Here’s what Rep. Stansbury has to say about her video.ARE YOU ALL READY FOR THIS???! 💙🔥 Because we are JUST GETTING STARTED!Do you know who else are ready to fight the current Republican regime? Many Republican lawmakers and allies alarmed by Tuesday’s wipeout are moving swiftly to pin blame for the election results on Hegseth, arguing behind the scenes that he played a chief role in convincing Trump to attack Iran with no exit strategy — and no plan for managing the inevitable political fallout.They’re not wrong about how we got bogged down in the Middle East. Piss-Drunk Pete absolutely snookered his demented boss, and filled his ears with fairy-tale nonsense about how he could bomb the shit out of Iran and be won and done in a couple of hours, with plenty of time left over for Pete to get soused down at the local bar.‘Drinnnkssss are on me, I just whupped Iran’s assssssss.’How did that work out for you, Pete? How did that work out for any of us?'Sucks to be you right now, Pete. They’re shoving you into a peach.House Republicans are expected to vote to directly repudiate the defense secretary in a matter of days. Rep. Thomas Massie of Kentucky, the famously anti-Trump GOP lawmaker, told CNN he plans to trigger a vote to impeach Hegseth when Congress returns next week — and multiple GOP sources said they expect it to pass.Leave it to Republicans to show us how it’s done. They’re not even waiting until the next Congress to stick their knives into their targets. They’re doing it Maybe Hakeem Jeffries might wan to take lessons from Thomas Massie. And now we must interrupt this post for an important message from Daughter Katie.I’m sure you love taking requests, so: you should use your platform to encourage people to call their new representatives and yell at them to demand they not put Jeffries and Schumer back in charge.Folks, Ms Spouse and I raised our daughter right, didn’t we? In fact, Katie is absolutely correct. We should all be calling our Reps and Senators (or their replacements) right now, and demanding leadership that will work to please , and not Morning Joe.All those phone numbers and shit can be found at the House and Senate web sites. Key Senate progressive Chris Van Hollen said Wednesday that Democrats should demand a “bold agenda” targeting entrenched corporate interests in Washington before agreeing to back Chuck Schumer or any other aspiring Senate majority leader.It’s our job to push — — them across the finish line.“Somebody came in, in the break there, and brought me a quote that we got from the president from the White House tonight, in response to the results, and I just threw it away. HA HA HA HA HA! That felt good, too. Guess what? It doesn’t matter. What do you think? Who has to care?”Ah, that glorious moment when you realize that Dear Leader We’re all about ready for some Daily Claudia now, right?Since Katie’s already made an appearance in this post, let’s continue the theme. Here she is with her mom in Newport, Rhode Island, early 1990s.This one’s at home, in the early 1990s.And, lastly, Katie in front of her house, with her mom, on June 20, 2018.Have a great Thursday, everyone.here’s your daily reminder that I can be found on Blue Sky at this link.this is going to be my closing message for the foreseeable future: do what you need to do to keep sane. if that means you need to disengage with my daily posts for a while, I get it. this community of ours will still be here when you return.to all the people who have signed on in the days since the election, . settle in as we all try to deal with the shitfuckery that’s ahead of us.we are all in this together, and we are all here for each other.

item.title: Mississippi Senate Update
item.author: Josh Marshall
item.source: Josh Marshall – TPM – Talking Points Memo
item.content:encoded: There’s a point of diminishing returns on non-definitive updates on the still outstanding Mississippi Senate race. But I’ve kept looking at the mix of outstanding votes, where they are, historical precedents, etc., and I’m pretty confident that Scott Colom is going to win this race and be the next senator from Mississippi. If it were callable it would be called. And it may take days or even a week to get a final verdict. But I just can’t find any argument that the remaining ballots don’t heavily favor Colom and he’s already up by almost 2,000 votes. (The AP numbers which most sites use are out of date.)Assuming that is true we’re likely looking at a 56-seat majority for the Democrats — technically 54 seats plus the two independents who caucus with the Democrats, if you want to be picky. That’s not only good news on its own for Democrats. It puts them in a good position to hold the Senate majority through the remainder of this decade.

item.title: Republicans Learn X Is the Echo Chamber
item.author: Matthew Gault
item.content:encoded: There's a BlazeTV YouTube video whose thumbnail shows the presenter with his arms around Anakin Skywalker and a gender-flipped Draco Malfoy called Malfoid. “Total Chud Victory?” It says. The video's title: “Young Right is Reclaiming Culture and Liberals Are Mad About it.”BlazeTV posted the video on November 2, the day before Democrats swept the midterms and started a political realignment in America so overwhelming that Republicans lost control of all the most powerful state positions in Texas.The video is a profound misreading of the political and cultural moment. It reminded me of stories of the Bolsheviks seizing the Winter Palace to discover tarot card playing courtiers who had no idea a revolution was happening in the streets.The American version was watching defense contractor Palmer Lucky dress up like Harry Potter on Halloween while standing . And it was Elon Musk — who spent roughly half a billion on the election only to see his chosen candidates fail — posting an AI generated picture of Anakin Skywalker sitting at the head of a happy fascist Star Wars family two days before the midterms.The online right has dominated American culture for a decade, or at least has dominated political narratives picked up by the mainstream media. Its memes and conspiracies drove news cycles. At first, the right’s memes filtered from random people on obscure Discord channels to Reddit’s r/the_donald or 4chan to Trump’s Twitter feed. More recently they’ve come from AI slop farms, from Musk, or from the administration itself. Powered by a well-funded media and podcast ecosystem, Fox News (and a propensity for shamelessness) its comedians, podcasters, and pundits became powerful celebrities and influencers, at least within Elon Musk’s X. This insular, often inscrutable world has given us Ben Shapiro, Nick Fuentes, Gamergate influencers, the streamer Asmongold, and a revolving door of characters who have shuffled interchangeably between Twitterverse celebritydom and actual government; Kash Patel, DataRepublican, Laura Loomer, Pete Hegseth, RFK Jr., Dan Bongino, the list goes on. It has been said many times that “Twitter is not real life,” and that posting too much anywhere will rot your brain. Never has that been more apparent than now: Much of Trumpworld spent the week before an election in which they would get utterly trounced using AI to generate barely legible Anakin and Malfoid memes for an inconsequential ingroup on the social media platform run by the biggest loser on the planet.“It certainly seems like it has had its high water mark and that reality has FINALLY caught up with the Republican Party,” Michael Senters, a PhD candidate at Virginia Tech who studies online and gaming culture, told 404 Media.In 2016, 4chan posters talked about — the pseudo-ironic belief that pictures on the internet could manifest great change in reality. According to legend, Trump strategist Steve Bannon was running a gold farm when he realized the angry gamers could be harnessed into a powerful reactionary political force. Bannon and others would successfully parlay Gamergate into an that’s dominated online life in the Trump era.During the midterm livestream of Bannon’s War Room podcast, his guest read exit polls that suggested the right-wing had lost young men — a group long thought to be its strongest soldiers. The split between the parties was even, the guest explained. “That can’t be right,” , signalling he’d lost touch with the constituency he’d harnessed on behalf of Trump ten years ago. As the election results began coming in, right-wing podcasters, livestreamers, and newscasters across the internet went through at least a few of the stages of grief. First they struggled to understand what was happening, suggesting the votes must be wrong. Eventually, many of them ragequit. "Okay, I'm going to be honest. I'm absolutely rage quitting. I'm so frustrated. I am so unbelievably frustrated. I'm so mad. I think Trump didn't do 50 different things he should have done. I think he should have gone a thousand times harder. I think that he wasted his time selling trinkets and nonsense,” Asmongold said as the returns came in. He lives in Texas where Democrats swept in a shock victory.“I wish that there were more people who thought like me that weren’t sorry about it. But you know what? There’s not. So it’s just me. And that’s fine. It’s fine. It’s OK,” he said, his voice catching in his throat.Many right-wing personalities went into Tuesday somehow expecting to win despite a disastrous war, a disastrous economy, disastrous polls, and a doddering president whose closing argument seemed to be more about his ballrooms, golf courses, and the than anything else. Since Trump was re-elected, these same people have called everyone else out of touch, convinced by their X algorithm and prediction markets that no blue wave would materialize. The media has similarly spent suggesting that Bluesky is an out-of-touch while mostly failing to suggest anything of the sort about the AI-pilled Silicon Valley executives, bots, and racists shitposting on X. Tuesday’s election wipeout highlights how detached from reality the Malfoid/Anakin-shipping, X-brained billionaires and their acolytes have actually become.“Blueskywave. Those of us on here, across the board, were out of touch. I see no other conclusion,” Joe Weisenthal of Bloomberg's Odd Lots podcast (who is a serious, good journalist), said in a after the election amidst a sea of Anakins tonguing Malfoids.The meme game and general demeanor of Trump and his followers has grown wildly tiresome in his thus far-disastrous second term. Under the guidance of White House Communications Director Steven Cheung, official government accounts have , used AI to put a studio Ghibli face on anti-immigrant propaganda, and fully embraced and as cultural heroes. The base on X loved this stuff. No one else did. As our friend Gita Jackson over at Aftermath wisely put it immediately before the election, "The idea that they can meme magic their way into a red sweep by posting about Anakin Skywalker a lot is pure desperation [...] Their values have been rejected by popular culture at large, and they are now resigned to exist in the margins.”Senters said the midterms showed the hard limits of memes as a political tool. “The power that memes have has always been, in my opinion, the power to help define linguistic and community lines in the amorphous space of the Internet. You create a community when you ‘get the joke’ behind a meme but memes generally don't persuade,” he said. “I'll be curious to see if the government accounts will continue to post these far-right cultural memes in the wake of the defeat or if they'll change their tune at all. Like do they double down on the meme posting to try to rally their base? Because it very clearly had ZERO appeal to anyone outside their base.”Yet the right-wing has spent the last ten years acting as if their memes had moved the country politically. “They deluded themselves into believing that memes carry persuasive power and that their bubble on X represented material reality in a meaningful way when that was no way close to the truth,” he said. “They saw how many ‘numbers’ the Malfoid and Anakin memes did on X and convinced themselves that this was a real cultural awakening moment and that the volk were on their side.”Alyssa Mercante, an internet culture reporter who is writing a book about politics and video games called , agreed. “I think what it's really showing is that when you start to get a little bit too deep in the weeds of this hyper online culture war stuff, it cannot escape the internet,” Mercante told 404 Media. “It is not working anymore. The material reality of America is just not good enough.” Gas prices are up. Everything is more expensive. And ICE has killed Americans in the streets. “This conspiratorial mindset is wrecker mentality. It is just destructive for the sake of destruction. There is no goal beyond pulling away any sort of legitimacy from the media or from democracy,” Mercante said. “When you get so deep in the weeds of this anti-establishment conspiratorial thought process, you just can't make anything or do anything of value. You're just upending tables and pointing at them and laughing.”Democrats crushed Republicans who leaned into the online culture war during the midterms. Bo French — an who ran for railroad commissioner in Texas — to voters that depicted himself as Master Chief from Halo. His opponent beat him by more than a million votes.In Nevada, composer Martin O’Donnell ran as a Republican for a House seat and lost to incumbent Susie Lee. O’Donnell announced his campaign on Discord and leaned hard into an extremely online gamer identity. “He’s like, ‘I wrote the music and I’m voting for Trump and you should too.’ He did a LAN party campaign fundraiser. The imagery was ,” Mercante said. “This dude is like: ‘, and they're resisting this [...] and Trump is the person that is going to help us resist,’ and he's polling like absolute dog water.”It’s been 12 years since Gamergate set the tempo for online culture wars and a decade since Trump won in 2016. In 2026, Star Wars, Halo, Harry Potter feel dated in a way they didn’t back then. “What 22-year-old kid is going to be like ‘they took from me.’ They don’t know to have it taken away from them,” Mercante said. She stressed that so much right wing online culture is about distraction — she likened it to jingling keys to capture the attention of a baby. “If the economy is the number one issue for both Democrats and Republicans going into the midterms, no amount of Malfoid scissoring Anakin Skywalker is going to change that need for people to be in a better financial position,” Mercante said. “The tech oligarchs pushed this stuff straight into our eyes for two years straight unfettered [...] And I wake up and gas is this expensive? I don’t care if you take a Taylor Swift song and make JD Vance walk out to it.”“[They] really thought that this would just last forever,” she added. “When you build up a meme presidency, eventually the cards just collapse underneath you, and there's just nothing to show for it.”Though this midterm signals a move away from Gamergate-style culture war politics, both Senters and Mercante cautioned that this type of rhetoric is still dangerous, and can still be destructive. “They’re still very good at doing propaganda on the internet — they wrote the book in many cases,” Mercante said.

item.title: An AI Fraud Kingpin’s Confessions
item.author: Joseph Cox
item.content:encoded: For months I’ve been speaking to an AI fraud kingpin. You might remember in 2024 we revealed the existence of OnlyFake, an underground site that let anyone generate realistic photos of fake IDs using ‘neural networks’. The creator of that site went by the handle John Wick. A while later, the creator was arrested.Turns out there was a lot more to that story. Yuriy Nazarenko, the creator of OnlyFake, told me his side of it. How when I published my initial article he panicked, and destroyed his laptop and emails and got a new phone, paranoid that authorities were about to bust down his door. How the pressure of a growing fraud empire pushed him to drugs. And how North Korean fake IT workers used his site. Read below for his story. A few years ago, Yuriy Nazarenko sat at a desk in his grandfather’s apartment in Ukraine and, on a diet of cigarettes, Lay’s chips, and beer, painstakingly made digital copies of fake identity documents. One of his four computer screens had the messaging app Telegram open. Another displayed a scan of a passport in Photoshop filling the entire monitor.Pixel by pixel, with rap music blaring, Nazarenko edited each part of the passport. That included the MRZ codes, the block of text printed at the bottom of identity documents; the photographs to superimpose someone else’s face into the document; and the overall dimensions and quirks of each different type of passport. Nazarenko would sometimes sit for more than 12 hours at his computer, obsessively tinkering away, with a single, high-quality fake identity document taking up to a week of work.When someone thinks of fake IDs, maybe they imagine a spotty underage teen buying a physical counterfeit drivers’ license so they can score some beer. But in the global criminal underworld, digital copies or scans of IDs are like a skeleton key. A convincing scan of an ID or utility bill, loaded with a bogus name or someone else’s identity, can unlock the ability to make bank accounts, bypass checks on cryptocurrency exchanges to buy or sell more Bitcoin, or rent a safehouse, all while keeping the criminal’s real identity hidden. The digitally altered IDs need to fool both human reviewers and automated systems that scan them for inconsistencies. Making fake IDs requires exquisite attention to detail.All of that manual labor doesn’t really scale, Nazarenko thought to himself as he meticulously edited passport after passport. He went on to make templates of fake identity documents that sped up the process, but it was still slow. After many of these quiet nights, he had an idea. He built a website to automate the process that autopopulated a fake ID with the personal data a customer wanted, rather than having him do it by hand. Then, when generative AI became mainstream a short while later, he incorporated that too.“That gradually became OnlyFake,” Nazarenko told me.OnlyFake, the underground website Nazarenko made, landed like a bomb in the fraud world. It allowed anyone to generate not only convincing scans of drivers’ licenses or passports, but also realistic looking photos of those fake identity documents laying on a sofa, carpet, or desk, as if someone had taken the ID out of their wallet and snapped a picture of it on their phone. Needed a convincing looking photo of a California drivers’ license to open a cryptocurrency account in someone else’s name? Or a British passport to incorporate a company overseas? Or a Social Security card? No problem. The results were photos of identity documents that didn’t really exist, of people who may not be real, but yet could trick the sorts of people and companies that verify documents.With OnlyFake, you didn’t have to be a master forger like Nazarenko to make fake documents. Now, anyone could churn out fake IDs at scale, sometimes even hundreds or thousands at a time. OnlyFake threatened the entire idea of know-your-customer, or KYC, where financial institutions take steps to know who exactly are using its services. When anyone can make a photo of a fake ID for just a few dollars in Bitcoin, is anyone really who they say they are?Nazarenko didn’t know it then, hunched over his desk, but OnlyFake would soon become so influential that it would spawn copy cats, and the FBI would eventually arrest Nazarenko and shut down some of its competitors. The Department of Justice said in an announcement about Nazarenko’s guilty plea that OnlyFake made more than a million dollars selling fake IDs for just $15 a pop.Now for the first time, Nazarenko, 28, free after a year in prison and living in Asia, is telling his story: how North Korean fake IT workers used his creation, how he ended up in ICE detention for months after serving his sentence in the U.S., and how OnlyFake unleashed a new age of AI-powered fraud. Nazarenko said he wanted to talk to me because I was the first journalist to reveal that OnlyFake existed. This article is based on interviews with Nazarenko and his lawyer; court records; and my own reporting in the online world of fraud that OnlyFake inhabited. “OnlyFake was the first time I saw how quickly a small internet project could turn into something global. Unfortunately, it also taught me, in a very painful way, what can happen when the scale of something grows faster than your understanding of its consequences,” Nazarenko told me.Growing up, Nazarenko’s parents questioned whether Nazarenko would ever find a job. His father worked for the Security Service of Ukraine. Raised in a suburb outside of Odesa, Nazarenko jumped between a few different gigs. He worked as a cook, a waiter, at a supermarket, and as a cameraman at a local Ukrainian TV station.We continued our election coverage with a piece from Matthew Gault . There were actually a ton of proposals related to data centers on the ballot in more than 40 races across 13 states. Well, people voted against data centers in at least 38 of them. People are sick of this stuff and they’re showing up to vote about it.If you know anything about music production, you’ll know that plugins for various pieces of software, like Ableton, are a big deal. This YouTube video goes through just how easy it is for someone to rip-off another’s painstakingly constructed plugin. These plugins can often emulate a particular guitar pedal, or a synthesizer, or whatever. Entire companies and solo developers make their income from selling plugins. Well, now anyone can make one.this insane video is going around OSINT and surveillance circles. Basically, it shows how the location of a video (and the person who took it) can be found by inaudible signals in the video and cross referencing this with aircraft data. I think? To be honest I need to watch it a few more times but check it out, this is nuts. The Binance hack is really terrifying. Maybe you’ve seen bits about the massive, $6 billion+ Binance hack, but details of how it went down are really crazy. You might already know it started with an employee talking to a fake company about a fake job offer and downloading malware (that is a big part of North Korea’s tactics). But there is another part I think is much, much scarier: the employee initially downloaded a malicious version of Homebrew that they found through a search engine, according to Binance’s writeup here. Homebrew, if you don’t know, is a massively widespread package manager for Macs. If you download something outside of the official App Store, or directly from a company’s site, you probably download it via Homebrew. This is especially common for developers. It’s basically the default. So, the hackers inserted themselves into one of the most common, and trusted, means for downloading software. That’s fucking scary! Here is the relevant section so you can see for yourself:“Engineer A from Wallet DevOps downloaded a tampered Homebrew installation in order to install a popular AI coding tool after searching for it on a search engine. Our security team detected the anomaly, replaced the device, and rotated all related credentials as a proactive security action. However, Engineer A’s role and his related colleagues on our wallet infrastructure team was exposed to the hacker.” The writeup that paragraph links to says it was a malicious ad. That’s just one part of the hack obviously, but it’s one that jumped out to me.Alright, that’s our newsletter for today. I’m off next week, so, if you excuse me, I’m off to play World of Warcraft.
